title.zh: 卷二百四十二 列傳第一 后妃上
title.raw: 卷二百四十二 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 242 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts 1

sentences.zh: 周人尊祖之詩曰：「厥初生民，時維姜嫄。

translations.literal: The Zhou people's poem honoring their ancestors says: "When the first people were born, it was Jiang Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou hymn honoring their ancestors we read: "When mankind first arose, the one was Lady Jiang Yuan."

sentences.zh: 」蓋推本后稷之所自出，以為王跡之所由基也。

translations.literal: " Thus they traced back to whence Hou Ji came forth, taking this as the foundation from which the royal enterprise arose.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they traced their descent back to the origins of Hou Ji, treating it as the foundation on which the royal mandate was laid.

sentences.zh: 宋之興，雖由先世積累，然至宣祖功業始大。

translations.literal: The rise of Song, though owing to accumulations of former generations, only at Grand Progenitor Xuanzu did meritorious achievement become great.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Song rise drew on generations of accumulated effort, it was not until the achievements of Grand Progenitor Xuanzu grew truly great.

sentences.zh: 昭憲杜后實生太祖、太宗，內助之賢，母範之正，蓋有以開宋世之基業者焉。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaoxian Du in fact bore Taizu and Taizong; the worth of her inner assistance and the rectitude of her maternal model surely had power to open the foundation of the Song age.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaoxian of the Du clan actually bore both Taizu and Taizong; in the worth of her support within the household and the rectitude of her example as a mother she plainly helped lay the foundations of the Song dynasty.

sentences.zh: 觀其訓太祖以《無逸》治天下，至於豫定太宗神器之傳，為宗社慮，蓋益遠矣。

translations.literal: Observing how she instructed Taizu to govern all under Heaven with "Against Dissipation," and even beforehand settled the transmission of the sacred regalia to Taizong, her consideration for the altars of state was still more far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how she taught Taizu to rule the realm by the precepts of "Against Dissipation," and even laid plans in advance for Taizong to receive the imperial succession—her foresight for the dynasty's altars reached still further.

sentences.zh: 厥後慈聖光獻曹后擁佑兩朝，宣聖烈高后垂簾聽政，而有元祐之治。

translations.literal: Thereafter Empress Cisheng Guangxian Cao supported and protected two reigns; Empress Xuanshenglie Gao held the curtain and heard government, and there was the governance of the Yuanyou era.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Empress Cisheng Guangxian of the Cao clan upheld two reigns, and Empress Xuanshenglie Gao ruled from behind the curtain—bringing forth the governance of the Yuanyou era.

sentences.zh: 南渡而後，若高宗之以母道事隆祐，孝宗奉明慈怡愉之樂，皆足以為百王法程。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, such matters as Gaozong's serving Longyou with the way of a son, and Xiaozong offering the joy of Bright Kindness and Pleasant Ease, are all sufficient to serve as models for the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south, Gaozong's treating Empress Longyou with a son's devotion and Xiaozong's devotion to Bright Kindness and Pleasant Ease stand as models worthy of the hundred sage-rulers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 宋三百餘年，外無漢王氏之患，內無唐武、韋之禍，豈不卓然而可尚哉。

translations.literal: Song for more than three hundred years had externally none of the Han Wang clan's calamity, internally none of the Tang Wu and Wei catastrophe—is this not outstanding and admirable?
translations.idiomatic: For more than three hundred years Song knew none of the Han Wang family's external domination nor the internal disasters of Tang's Wu and Wei—surely this is outstanding and worthy of admiration.

sentences.zh: 昭憲垂裕之功，至是茂矣。

translations.literal: Zhaoxian's work of bequeathing abundance, by this time had become luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: By then the abundant legacy left by Empress Zhaoxian had fully flourished.

sentences.zh: 舊史稱昭憲性嚴毅，有禮法。

translations.literal: The old histories say Zhaoxian's nature was stern and resolute, with ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: The old histories describe Empress Zhaoxian as stern and disciplined, observant of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 《易》之《家人》上九曰：「有孚，威如，終吉。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes, "The Family," top nine says: "There is sincerity; awe-inspiring, and in the end good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The top line of "The Family" in the Book of Changes reads: "With inner sincerity, awe-inspiring authority—in the end, good fortune."

sentences.zh: 」其是之謂歟。

translations.literal: " Is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not exactly what is meant?

sentences.zh: 作《后妃傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was composed the "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts."

sentences.zh: 太祖母 昭憲杜太后

translations.literal: Grandmother of the Throne: Empress Zhaoxian Dowager Du
translations.idiomatic: Grandmother of the Throne: Empress Zhaoxian Dowager Du

sentences.zh: 太祖母昭憲杜太后，定州安喜人也。

translations.literal: The Grandmother of the Throne, Empress Zhaoxian Dowager Du, was a native of Anxi in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Grandmother of the Throne, Empress Zhaoxian Dowager Du, was a native of Anxi in Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父爽，贈太師。

translations.literal: Her father Shuang was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shuang was posthumously ennobled as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 母範氏，生五子三女，太后居長。

translations.literal: Her mother was of the Fan clan; she bore five sons and three daughters, and the Empress Dowager was the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was of the Fan clan; she bore five sons and three daughters, and the Empress Dowager was the eldest.

sentences.zh: 既笄歸於宣祖。

translations.literal: After coming of age she was married to Grand Progenitor Xuanzu.
translations.idiomatic: After she came of age she was married to Grand Progenitor Xuanzu.

sentences.zh: 治家嚴毅有禮法。

translations.literal: She managed the household with stern discipline and observance of ritual law.
translations.idiomatic: She ran the household with stern discipline and strict observance of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 生邕王光濟、太祖、太宗、秦王廷美、夔王光贊、燕國陳國二長公主。

translations.literal: She bore Prince of Yong Guangji, Taizu, Taizong, Prince of Qin Tingmei, Prince of Kui Guangzan, and the two elder princesses of Yan and Chen states.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Prince of Yong Guangji, Taizu, Taizong, Prince of Qin Tingmei, Prince of Kui Guangzan, and the two elder princesses of Yan and Chen.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，太后不豫，太祖侍樂餌不離左右。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong the Empress Dowager was unwell; Taizu attended her with food and medicine, never leaving her side.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong the Empress Dowager fell ill; Taizu waited on her with food and medicine and never left her side.

sentences.zh: 疾亟，召趙普入受遺命。

translations.literal: When her illness grew critical she summoned Zhao Pu to receive her final testament.
translations.idiomatic: When her illness grew critical she summoned Zhao Pu to receive her final instructions.

sentences.zh: 太后因問太祖曰：「汝知所以得天下乎？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager thereupon asked Taizu, "Do you know by what means you obtained all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then asked Taizu, "Do you know how you came to win the empire?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖嗚噎不能對。

translations.literal: " Taizu sobbed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sobbed and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 太后固問之，太祖曰：「臣所以得天下者，皆祖考及太后之積慶也。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager pressed the question; Taizu said, "Your subject obtained all under Heaven entirely through the accumulated blessings of his ancestors and the Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager pressed him again. Taizu said, "I won the empire solely through the accumulated blessings of my forebears and of Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「不然，正由周世宗使幼兒主天下耳。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager said, "It is not so; it was precisely because Emperor Shizong of Zhou set a child to rule all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "That is not so. It was precisely because Emperor Shizong of Zhou left a child on the throne."

sentences.zh: 使周氏有長君，天下豈為汝有乎？

translations.literal: Had the Zhou house had a mature ruler, would all under Heaven have been yours?
translations.idiomatic: If the Zhou house had had a mature ruler, would the empire ever have become yours?

sentences.zh: 汝百歲後當傳位於汝弟。

translations.literal: When you reach a hundred years you should transmit the throne to your younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: When your time comes you must pass the throne to your younger brother.

sentences.zh: 四海至廣，萬幾至眾，能立長君，社稷之福也。

translations.literal: The four seas are exceedingly broad and the myriad affairs exceedingly numerous; to be able to establish a mature ruler is the blessing of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is vast and state affairs are countless; to place a mature ruler on the throne is a blessing for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」太祖頓首泣曰：「敢不如教。

translations.literal: " Taizu bowed his head to the ground and wept, saying, "I dare not fail to follow the instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu bowed his head to the ground and wept. "I shall not fail to obey," he said.

sentences.zh: 」太后顧謂趙普曰：「爾同記吾言，不可違也。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager turned and said to Zhao Pu, "You likewise record my words; they must not be violated."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager turned to Zhao Pu. "You too must record my words," she said. "They must not be disobeyed."

sentences.zh: 」命普於榻前為約誓書，普於紙尾書「臣普書」。

translations.literal: " She ordered Pu to draft a covenant oath before the couch; Pu wrote at the end of the paper, "Your subject Pu writes."
translations.idiomatic: She ordered Pu to draft a sworn covenant at her bedside; at the foot of the document Pu wrote, "Written by your subject Pu."

sentences.zh: 藏之金匱，命謹密宮人掌之。

translations.literal: It was stored in a golden coffer, and she ordered discreet palace women to keep charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: The document was placed in a golden coffer and entrusted to trustworthy palace women for safekeeping.

sentences.zh: 太后崩于滋德殿，年六十，諡曰明憲。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager died in Zide Hall at the age of sixty; her posthumous title was Mingxian.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager died in Zide Hall at the age of sixty and was given the posthumous title Mingxian.

sentences.zh: 葬安陵，神主祔享太廟。

translations.literal: She was buried at Anling; her spirit tablet was enshrined for joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Anling, and her spirit tablet was installed for joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，更諡昭憲，合祔安陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande her title was changed to Zhaoxian, and she was jointly enshrined at Anling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande her posthumous title was changed to Zhaoxian, and she was enshrined together at Anling.

sentences.zh: 孝惠賀皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiaohui He
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaohui of the He Clan

sentences.zh: 孝明王皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoming Wang
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoming of the Wang Clan

sentences.zh: 孝明王皇后，邠州新平人。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoming Wang was a native of Xinping in Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoming of the Wang clan was a native of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彰德軍節度饒第三女。

translations.literal: She was the third daughter of Rao, military commissioner of Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: She was the third daughter of Rao, military commissioner of the Zhangde Army.

sentences.zh: 孝惠崩，周顯德五年，太祖為殿前檢點校，聘后為繼室。

translations.literal: When Xiaohui died, in the fifth year of Xiande of Zhou Taizu was inspector-in-chief of the Palace Front Office and betrothed the Empress as his successor consort.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Xiaohui's death, in the fifth year of Xiande of Zhou, while Taizu was inspector-in-chief of the Palace Front Office, he took her as his successor consort.

sentences.zh: 后恭勤不懈，仁慈禦下。

translations.literal: The Empress was respectful and diligent without slackening, benevolent in governing those below.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was respectful and tireless in her duties, and governed those below her with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 周世宗賜冠帔，封琅邪郡夫人。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong of Zhou bestowed cap and veil upon her and enfeoffed her as Lady of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Zhou granted her cap and veil and ennobled her as Lady of Langye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，建隆元年八月，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, in the eighth month of the first year of Jianlong she was invested as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, in the eighth month of the first year of Jianlong she was invested as Empress.

sentences.zh: 常服寬衣，佐禦膳，善彈箏鼓琴。

translations.literal: She regularly wore plain wide garments, assisted at the imperial meals, and was skilled at playing the zither, drum, and qin.
translations.idiomatic: She habitually wore simple, loose garments, helped supervise the imperial meals, and was skilled at the zither, drum, and qin.

sentences.zh: 晨起，誦佛書。

translations.literal: Rising in the morning, she recited Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning she rose early to recite Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 事杜太后得驩心。

translations.literal: In serving Empress Dowager Du she won delight.
translations.idiomatic: In serving Empress Dowager Du she won her heartfelt affection.

sentences.zh: 生子女三人，皆夭。

translations.literal: She bore three sons and daughters, all of whom died young.
translations.idiomatic: She bore three children, all of whom died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年十二月崩，年二十二。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Qiande she died at the age of twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the twelfth month of the first year of Qiande at the age of twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 有司上諡，翰林學士竇儀撰哀冊文。

translations.literal: The responsible offices submitted a posthumous title; Hanlin academician Dou Yi composed the lamentation eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed a posthumous title, and Hanlin academician Dou Yi composed the lamentation eulogy.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，葬安陵之北。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year she was buried north of Anling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year she was buried north of Anling.

sentences.zh: 神主享於別廟。

translations.literal: Her spirit tablet received sacrifice in a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: Her spirit tablet was enshrined for sacrifice in a separate temple.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，祔享太廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo she was enshrined for joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo her spirit tablet was installed for joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 孝章宋皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiaozhang Song
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaozhang of the Song Clan

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，居西宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo she resided in the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo she took up residence in the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，移居東宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi she moved to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongxi she moved to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 至道元年四月崩，年四十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhidao she died at the age of forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fourth month of the first year of Zhidao at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 有司上諡，權殯普濟佛舍。

translations.literal: The responsible offices submitted a posthumous title; provisionally she was interred at Puji Buddhist lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed a posthumous title, and her body was provisionally interred at the Puji Buddhist lodge.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，祔葬永昌陵北。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year she was buried in joint sepulture north of Yongchang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year she was buried in joint sepulture north of Yongchang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 命吏部侍郎李至撰哀冊文，神主享於別廟。

translations.literal: He ordered Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Li Zhi to compose the lamentation eulogy; her spirit tablet received sacrifice in a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Vice Minister of Personnel Li Zhi to compose the lamentation eulogy, and her spirit tablet was enshrined for sacrifice in a separate temple.

sentences.zh: 神宗時，升祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the time of Shenzong she was elevated for joint enshrinement in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong her spirit tablet was elevated for joint enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 淑德尹皇后

translations.literal: Empress Shude Yin
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shude of the Yin Clan

sentences.zh: 太宗淑德尹皇后，相州鄴人。

translations.literal: Taizong's Empress Shude Yin was a native of Ye in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's Empress Shude of the Yin clan was a native of Ye in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 滁州刺史廷勳之女。

translations.literal: She was the daughter of Tingxun, prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of Tingxun, prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 兄崇珂，保信軍節度。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Chongke was military commissioner of Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Chongke was military commissioner of the Baoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 太宗在周時娶焉。

translations.literal: Taizong married her while still under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong married her while he was still serving the Zhou regime.

sentences.zh: 早薨。

translations.literal: She died early.
translations.idiomatic: She died young.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，詔追冊為皇后，並諡，葬孝明陵西北。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, an edict posthumously invested her as Empress, together with a posthumous title; she was buried northwest of Xiaoming Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, an edict posthumously invested her as Empress and granted her a posthumous title; she was buried northwest of Xiaoming Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 神主享於別廟，后升祔太廟。

translations.literal: Her spirit tablet received sacrifice in a separate temple; later she was elevated for joint enshrinement in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Her spirit tablet was enshrined in a separate temple; later she was elevated for joint enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 懿德符皇后

translations.literal: Empress Yide Fu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yide of the Fu Clan

sentences.zh: 明德李皇后

translations.literal: Empress Mingde Li
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mingde of the Li Clan

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，真宗即位。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, Zhenzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, Zhenzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 至道三年四月，尊后為皇太后，居西宮嘉慶殿。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Zhidao the Empress was honored as Empress Dowager and resided in Jiqing Hall of the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Zhidao the Empress was honored as Empress Dowager and took up residence in Jiqing Hall of the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，宰相請別建宮立名，從之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping the chief ministers requested that a separate palace be built and named; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping the chief ministers asked that a separate palace be built and given its own name, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 四年宮成，移居之，仍上宮名曰萬安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the palace was completed; she moved there, and moreover submitted that the palace be named Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the palace was completed and she moved there; she also proposed that the palace be named Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 景德元年崩，年四十五。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde she died at the age of forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the first year of Jingde at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡明德。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title Mingde.

sentences.zh: 權殯沙台。

translations.literal: Provisionally she was interred at Shatai.
translations.idiomatic: Her body was provisionally interred at Shatai.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，祔葬永熙陵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year she was buried in joint sepulture at Yongxi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year she was buried in joint sepulture at Yongxi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 禮官請以懿德、明德同祔太宗廟室，以先後為次，從之。

translations.literal: The ritual officials requested that Yide and Mingde be jointly enshrined in Taizong's temple chamber, ordered by precedence of earlier and later; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials asked that Empresses Yide and Mingde be jointly enshrined in Taizong's temple chamber in order of precedence, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 元德李皇后

translations.literal: Empress Yuande Li
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuande of the Li Clan

sentences.zh: 李賢妃，真定人，乾州防禦使英之女也。

translations.literal: Consort Li the Worthy was a native of Zhending, daughter of Ying, defense commissioner of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li the Worthy was a native of Zhending and the daughter of Ying, defense commissioner of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，追封賢妃，又進上尊號為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Worthy Consort, and further advanced in honored title to Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Worthy Consort and further honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 有司上諡曰元德。

translations.literal: The responsible offices submitted the posthumous title Yuande.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed the posthumous title Yuande.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，祔葬永熙陵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping she was buried in joint sepulture at Yongxi Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping she was buried in joint sepulture at Yongxi Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、平章事李沆為園陵使。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor Li Hang was appointed mausoleum commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor Li Hang was appointed commissioner of the imperial mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 車駕詣普安院攢宮，素服行禮，拜伏嗚咽。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage went to the temporary palace at Pu'an Monastery; in plain garments he performed the rites, bowing prostrate and sobbing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to the temporary palace at Pu'an Monastery, performed the rites in plain mourning garments, and bowed prostrate, weeping aloud.

sentences.zh: 命駕部郎中、知制誥梁周翰撰哀冊。

translations.literal: He ordered Secretariat Drafter Liang Zhouhan, Bureau Director of the Imperial Transport Office, to compose the lamentation eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liang Zhouhan of the Imperial Transport Office, drafter of imperial documents, to compose the lamentation eulogy.

sentences.zh: 神主祔別廟。

translations.literal: Her spirit tablet was enshrined in a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: Her spirit tablet was installed for sacrifice in a separate temple.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，追贈后父英檢校太尉、安國軍節度、常山郡王，母魏國太夫人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu the Empress's father Ying was posthumously enfeoffed as acting Grand Marshal, military commissioner of Anguo Army, and Prince of Changshan Commandery; her mother as Grand Lady of Wei State.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu the Empress's father Ying was posthumously enfeoffed as acting Grand Marshal, military commissioner of the Anguo Army, and Prince of Changshan Commandery; her mother as Grand Lady of Wei.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，禮官趙湘請以后祔太宗廟室。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu the ritual official Zhao Xiang requested that the Empress be jointly enshrined in Taizong's temple chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu the ritual official Zhao Xiang asked that the Empress be jointly enshrined in Taizong's temple chamber.

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「此重事也，俟令禮官議之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong said, "This is a weighty matter; wait until the ritual officials are ordered to deliberate on it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong said, "This is a weighty matter. Let the ritual officials deliberate on it first."

sentences.zh: 」六年秋，宰相王旦與群臣表請后尊號中去「太」字，升祔太廟明德之次，從之。

translations.literal: " In the autumn of the sixth year Grand Councilor Wang Dan and the officials memorialized requesting that the character "Grand" be removed from the Empress's honored title, and that she be elevated for joint enshrinement in the Grand Temple after Mingde; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year Grand Councilor Wang Dan and the officials memorialized asking that the character "Grand" be removed from the Empress's honored title and that she be elevated for joint enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple after Mingde; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 章懷潘皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhanghuai Pan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhanghuai of the Pan Clan

sentences.zh: 真宗章懷潘皇后，大名人，忠武軍節度美第八女。

translations.literal: Zhenzong's Empress Zhanghuai Pan was a native of Daming, the eighth daughter of Mei, military commissioner of Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong's Empress Zhanghuai of the Pan clan was a native of Daming and the eighth daughter of Mei, military commissioner of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 真宗在韓邸，太宗為聘之，封莒國夫人。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was at the Han residence, Taizong betrothed her to him and enfeoffed her as Lady of Ju State.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhenzong was still at the Han residence, Taizong betrothed her to him and enfeoffed her as Lady of Ju.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年五月薨，年二十二。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Duangong she died at the age of twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fifth month of the second year of Duangong at the age of twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，追冊為皇后，諡壯懷，葬永昌陵之側，陵名保泰。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, she was posthumously invested as Empress with the posthumous title Zhuanghuai; she was buried beside Yongchang Mausoleum, the mausoleum named Baotai.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, she was posthumously invested as Empress with the posthumous title Zhuanghuai and buried beside Yongchang Mausoleum in a tomb named Baotai.

sentences.zh: 神主享於別廟，舊制后諡冠以帝諡。

translations.literal: Her spirit tablet received sacrifice in a separate temple; by old regulation an empress's posthumous title was prefixed with the emperor's posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Her spirit tablet was enshrined in a separate temple. By established custom an empress's posthumous title was prefixed with her husband's temple name.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，禮官言，「孝」字連太祖諡，「德」字連太宗諡。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era the ritual officials said that the character "Xiao" linked to Taizu's posthumous title and the character "De" linked to Taizong's posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era the ritual officials observed that the character xiao linked to Taizu's temple title and the character de linked to Taizong's temple title.

sentences.zh: 遂改「壯」為「章」，以連真宗諡云。

translations.literal: Thereupon they changed "Zhuang" to "Zhang," to link with Zhenzong's posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore changed zhuang to zhang so that her title would link with Zhenzong's temple name.

sentences.zh: 章穆郭皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhangmu Guo
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangmu of the Guo Clan

sentences.zh: 章穆郭皇后，太原人，宣徽南院便守文第二女。

translations.literal: Empress Zhangmu Guo was a native of Taiyuan, the second daughter of Shouwen, deputy of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangmu of the Guo clan was a native of Taiyuan and the second daughter of Shouwen, deputy of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，真宗在襄邸，太宗為聘之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, while Zhenzong was at the Xiang residence, Taizong betrothed her to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua, while Zhenzong was still at the Xiang residence, Taizong betrothed her to him.

sentences.zh: 封魯國夫人，進封秦國。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Lady of Lu State and advanced to Lady of Qin State.
translations.idiomatic: She was enfeoffed as Lady of Lu and later advanced to Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, she was established as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, she was made Empress.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，從幸西京還，以疾崩，年三十二。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, returning from accompanying the emperor on a visit to the Western Capital, she died of illness at the age of thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingde, on the return from accompanying the emperor to the Western Capital, she died of illness at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 后謙約惠下，性惡奢靡。

translations.literal: The Empress was modest and restrained, gracious to those below, and by nature detested extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was modest and gracious to those below her and detested extravagance by nature.

sentences.zh: 族屬入謁禁中，服飾華侈，必加戒勖。

translations.literal: When kinsmen entered the palace to pay homage, if their dress was sumptuous she always admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: When relatives came to the palace to pay homage in lavish dress, she always admonished them.

sentences.zh: 有以家事求言於上者，后終不許。

translations.literal: If anyone sought to speak to the sovereign on family affairs, the Empress never permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone sought to speak to the emperor on family affairs, the Empress never allowed it.

sentences.zh: 兄子出嫁，以貧欲祈恩賚，但出裝具給之。

translations.literal: When her brother's son married, wishing because of poverty to beg imperial favor, she only provided trousseau and furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: When her brother's son married, he wished to beg imperial favor because of poverty, but she gave him only trousseau and furnishings.

sentences.zh: 上尤加禮重。

translations.literal: The sovereign especially added ritual honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated her with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 及崩，上深嗟悼。

translations.literal: When she died, the sovereign deeply sighed in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, the emperor mourned her deeply.

sentences.zh: 禮官奏皇帝七日釋服，特詔增至十三日。

translations.literal: The ritual officials memorialized that the emperor should lay aside mourning garments after seven days; a special edict increased this to thirteen days.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials proposed that the emperor lay aside mourning after seven days, but a special edict extended the period to thirteen days.

sentences.zh: 太常上諡曰壯穆。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted the posthumous title Zhuangmu.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous title Zhuangmu.

sentences.zh: 靈駕發引，命翰林學士楊億撰哀冊。

translations.literal: When the spirit carriage set out, he ordered Hanlin academician Yang Yi to compose the lamentation eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession set out, he ordered Hanlin academician Yang Yi to compose the lamentation eulogy.

sentences.zh: 葬永熙陵之西北，神主享於別廟。

translations.literal: She was buried northwest of Yongxi Mausoleum; her spirit tablet received sacrifice in a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried northwest of Yongxi Mausoleum, and her spirit tablet was enshrined for sacrifice in a separate temple.

sentences.zh: 以后弟崇儀副使崇仁為壯宅使、康州刺史，侄承慶、承壽皆遷官。

translations.literal: The Empress's younger brother Chongren, deputy commissioner of the Chongyi Office, was made Zhuangzhai commissioner and prefect of Kangzhou; her nephews Chengqing and Chengshou were all promoted in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress's younger brother Chongren, deputy commissioner of the Chongyi Office, was appointed commissioner of the Zhuangzhai estate and prefect of Kangzhou; her nephews Chengqing and Chengshou were all promoted.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，封后母高唐郡太夫人梁氏萊國太夫人。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era the Empress's mother, Grand Lady of Gaotang Commandery of the Liang clan, was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Lai State.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era the Empress's mother, Grand Lady of Gaotang Commandery of the Liang clan, was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Lai.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，升祔真宗廟室，改諡章穆。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, she was elevated for joint enshrinement in Zhenzong's temple chamber, and her title was changed to Zhangmu.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, she was elevated for joint enshrinement in Zhenzong's temple chamber and her posthumous title was changed to Zhangmu.

sentences.zh: 章獻明肅劉皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhangxian Mingsu Liu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangxian Mingsu of the Liu Clan

sentences.zh: 章獻明肅劉皇后，其先家太原，後徙益州，為華陽人。

translations.literal: Empress Zhangxian Mingsu Liu: her forebears' home was Taiyuan; later they moved to Yizhou and became natives of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangxian Mingsu of the Liu clan: her family originally came from Taiyuan, later moved to Yizhou, and became natives of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 祖延慶，在晉、漢間為右驍衛大將軍；

translations.literal: Her grandfather Yanqing, between Jin and Han, was Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Yanqing served between the Jin and Han regimes as Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guard;

sentences.zh: 父通，虎捷都指揮使、嘉州刺史，從征太原，道卒。

translations.literal: her father Tong was commander-in-chief of the Tiger Swift Army and prefect of Jiazhou; accompanying the campaign against Taiyuan, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: her father Tong was commander-in-chief of the Tiger Swift Army and prefect of Jiazhou; he died on campaign against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 后，通第二女也。

translations.literal: The Empress was Tong's second daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was Tong's second daughter.

sentences.zh: 自章穆崩，真宗欲立為皇后，大臣多以為不可，帝卒立之。

translations.literal: After Zhangmu died, Zhenzong wished to establish her as Empress; many chief ministers held this impossible, but the Emperor in the end established her.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Zhangmu's death, Zhenzong wished to make her Empress; many chief ministers opposed it, but he established her in the end.

sentences.zh: 李宸妃生仁宗，后以為己子，與楊淑妃撫禮甚至。

translations.literal: Consort Li the Imperial bore Renzong; the Empress took him as her own son and, with Consort Yang the Gracious, nurtured and honored him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li the Imperial bore Renzong; the Empress took him as her own son and, together with Consort Yang the Gracious, raised him with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 后性警悟，曉書史，聞朝廷事，能記其本末。

translations.literal: The Empress's nature was alert and perceptive; she understood books and histories, and hearing court affairs could remember their beginnings and ends.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was quick-witted and well read; when she heard of court affairs she could recall them from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 真宗退朝，閱天下封奏，多至中夜，后皆預聞。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong left court and reviewed memorials from all under Heaven, often until midnight, the Empress was always forewarned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong left court to review memorials from across the realm, often until midnight, the Empress was always informed beforehand.

sentences.zh: 宮圍事有問，輒傅引故實以對。

translations.literal: If palace matters were questioned, she would at once cite precedents in reply.
translations.idiomatic: When palace matters were questioned, she would cite historical precedents in reply.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，帝久疾居宮中，事多決於后。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi the Emperor was long ill and dwelt in the palace; many affairs were decided by the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianxi the emperor was long ill and confined to the palace; many affairs were decided by the Empress.

sentences.zh: 宰相上寇凖密議奏請皇太子監國，以謀泄罷相，用丁謂代之。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Kou Zhun secretly discussed and memorialized requesting that the Crown Prince oversee the state; because the plot leaked he was dismissed as councilor and Ding Wei was used in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Kou Zhun secretly memorialized asking that the crown prince oversee the state; when the plot leaked he was dismissed and Ding Wei replaced him.

sentences.zh: 既而，入內都知周懷政謀廢后殺謂，復用凖以輔太子。

translations.literal: Thereafter Palace Intendant Zhou Huaizheng plotted to depose the Empress and kill Wei, and restore Kou to assist the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Palace Intendant Zhou Huaizheng plotted to depose the Empress, kill Ding Wei, and restore Kou Zhun to assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 客省使楊崇勳、內殿承制楊懷吉詣謂告，謂夜乘犢車，挾崇勳、懷吉造樞密使曹利用謀。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Reception Bureau Yang Chongxun and Inner Hall Attendant Yang Huaiji went to inform Wei; Wei at night rode a calf cart, taking Chongxun and Huaiji to visit Military Affairs Commissioner Cao Liyong to plot.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Yang Chongxun of the Reception Bureau and Inner Hall Attendant Yang Huaiji informed Ding Wei; that night Wei rode in a calf cart with them to Military Affairs Commissioner Cao Liyong to plot.

sentences.zh: 明日，誅懷政，貶准衡州司馬。

translations.literal: The next day Huaizheng was executed and Zhun was demoted to military aide of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Huaizheng was executed and Kou Zhun was demoted to military aide of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是詔皇太子開資善堂，引大臣決天下事，后裁制於內。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Crown Prince to open the Hall of Nurturing Goodness, summoning chief ministers to decide affairs of all under Heaven, while the Empress adjudicated within.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the crown prince to open the Hall of Nurturing Goodness, summoning chief ministers to decide state affairs while the Empress ruled from within.

sentences.zh: 真宗崩，遺詔尊后為皇太后，軍國重事，權取處分。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong died, the testamentary edict honored the Empress as Empress Dowager; on weighty military and state affairs she was empowered to decide provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong died, his testamentary edict honored the Empress as Empress Dowager and empowered her to decide provisionally on weighty military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 謂等請太后御別殿，太后遣張景宗、雷允恭諭曰：「皇帝視事，當朝夕在側，何須別御一殿？

translations.literal: Wei and others requested that the Empress Dowager attend a separate hall; the Empress Dowager sent Zhang Jingzong and Lei Yungong to instruct, saying, "When the Emperor conducts affairs of state, he should be at one's side morning and evening—why need a separate hall?"
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei and others asked the Empress Dowager to hold court in a separate hall. She sent Zhang Jingzong and Lei Yungong to say, "When the emperor conducts affairs of state he should be at my side morning and evening—why need a separate hall?"

sentences.zh: 」於是請帝與太后五日一御承明殿，帝位左，太后位右，垂簾決事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they requested that the Emperor and Empress Dowager every five days attend Chenming Hall, the Emperor's seat on the left and the Empress Dowager's on the right, with the curtain drawn to decide affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They then proposed that the emperor and Empress Dowager attend Chenming Hall every five days, the emperor seated on the left and the Empress Dowager on the right, with a curtain drawn between them to decide affairs.

sentences.zh: 議已定，太后忽出手書，第欲禁中閱章奏，遇大事即召對輔臣。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was settled, the Empress Dowager suddenly produced a handwritten note, wishing only to review memorials within the palace, and on great affairs to summon and face chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After the plan was settled, the Empress Dowager suddenly produced a handwritten note saying she wished only to review memorials within the palace and summon chief ministers for great affairs.

sentences.zh: 其謀出於丁謂，非太后意也。

translations.literal: This plot came from Ding Wei; it was not the Empress Dowager's intent.
translations.idiomatic: This scheme came from Ding Wei, not from the Empress Dowager herself.

sentences.zh: 謂既貶，馮拯等三上奏，請如初議。

translations.literal: After Wei was demoted, Feng Zheng and others thrice memorialized, requesting the original deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: After Ding Wei was demoted, Feng Zheng and others memorialized three times asking to return to the original plan.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以為言，於是始同御承明殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor also spoke to this effect; thereupon they first jointly attended Chenming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke in favor of it as well, and they began jointly to attend Chenming Hall.

sentences.zh: 百官表賀，太后哀慟。

translations.literal: The hundred officials memorialized congratulations; the Empress Dowager mourned in grief.
translations.idiomatic: The officials memorialized their congratulations, but the Empress Dowager grieved in mourning.

sentences.zh: 有司請制令稱「吾」，以生日為長寧節，出入御大安輦，鳴鞭侍衛如乘輿。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested that edicts address her as "I," that her birthday be made Changning Festival, that going in and out she ride the Great Peace imperial carriage, and that whips be cracked and guards attend as when riding the imperial chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices asked that edicts address her as "I," that her birthday be made the Changning Festival, that she ride the Great Peace imperial carriage when going out, and that guards attend her with the same ceremony as the emperor.

sentences.zh: 令天下避太后父諱。

translations.literal: They ordered all under Heaven to avoid the Empress Dowager's father's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered the realm to observe taboo on the Empress Dowager's father's name.

sentences.zh: 群臣上尊號曰「應元崇德仁壽慈聖太后」，御文德殿受冊。

translations.literal: The officials submitted the honored title "Empress Dowager Responding to the Primordial, Honoring Virtue, Benevolent in Longevity, Merciful and Sagely," and she received the investiture at Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The officials submitted the honored title "Empress Dowager Responding to the Primordial, Honoring Virtue, Benevolent in Longevity, Merciful and Sagely," and she received investiture at Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 天聖五年正旦，太后御會慶殿。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the fifth year of Tiansheng the Empress Dowager attended Huiqing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the fifth year of Tiansheng the Empress Dowager held court at Huiqing Hall.

sentences.zh: 群臣及契丹使者班廷中，帝再拜跪上壽。

translations.literal: The officials and Khitan envoys formed ranks in the hall; the Emperor twice bowed and knelt to offer longevity wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and Khitan envoys formed ranks in the hall while the emperor bowed twice and knelt to offer birthday wishes.

sentences.zh: 是歲郊祀前，出手書諭百官，毋請加尊號。

translations.literal: Before the suburban sacrifice that year, she produced a handwritten note instructing the hundred officials not to request an added honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Before the suburban sacrifice that year she sent a handwritten note instructing officials not to request an additional honored title.

sentences.zh: 禮成，帝率百官恭謝如元日。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, the Emperor led the hundred officials in respectful thanks as on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, the emperor led the officials in respectful thanks as on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 七年冬至，天子又率百官上壽，范仲淹力言其非，不聽。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice of the seventh year the Son of Heaven again led the hundred officials to offer longevity wishes; Fan Zhongyan strongly spoke that this was wrong, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice of the seventh year the emperor again led officials to offer birthday wishes; Fan Zhongyan strongly objected, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔長寧節百官賜衣，天下賜宴，皆如乾元節。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict ordered that on Changning Festival the hundred officials receive gift garments and all under Heaven receive banquets, all as on Qianyuan Festival.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict ordered that on the Changning Festival officials receive gift garments and banquets be held throughout the realm, all as on the Qianyuan Festival.

sentences.zh: 是歲崩，年六十五。

translations.literal: That year she died at the age of sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That year she died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡曰章獻明肅，葬於永定陵之西北。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Zhangxian Mingsu; she was buried northwest of Yongding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title Zhangxian Mingsu and buried northwest of Yongding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 舊制皇后皆二諡，稱制，加四諡自后始。

translations.literal: By old regulation empresses all had two posthumous titles; ruling as regent and adding four posthumous titles began with this Empress.
translations.idiomatic: By established custom empresses received two posthumous titles; the addition of four titles while ruling as regent began with her.

sentences.zh: 追贈三世皆至太師、尚書令、兼中書令，父封魏王。

translations.literal: Posthumous enfeoffments for three generations all reached Grand Preceptor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat; her father was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of forebears were posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat; her father was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，仁宗即位尚少，太后稱制，雖政出宮闈，而號令嚴明，恩威加天下。

translations.literal: At first, when Renzong ascended the throne he was still young; the Empress Dowager ruled as regent. Though government issued from the women's quarters, her commands were stern and clear, and favor and awe extended over all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong first took the throne he was still young, and the Empress Dowager ruled as regent. Though government issued from the inner palace, her commands were stern and clear and her authority extended across the realm.

sentences.zh: 左右近習亦少所假借，宮掖間未嘗妄改作。

translations.literal: Those close at hand were also seldom indulged; within the palace quarters there was never reckless alteration or construction.
translations.idiomatic: Those close to her were seldom indulged, and within the palace quarters there was never reckless alteration or construction.

sentences.zh: 內外賜與有節，柴氏、李氏二公主入見，猶服髲鬀。

translations.literal: Internal and external grants were measured; when the two princesses of the Chai and Li clans came to audience they still wore wig coiffure.
translations.idiomatic: Grants within and outside the palace were restrained; when the two princesses of the Chai and Li clans came to audience they still wore wig coiffures.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「姑老矣。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Your aunt is old."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Your aunt is old."

sentences.zh: 」命左右賜以珠璣帕首。

translations.literal: " She ordered those at hand to bestow pearl and jade headcloths.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered attendants to bestow pearl and jade headcloths on them.

sentences.zh: 時潤王元份婦安國夫人李氏老，髮且落，見太后，亦請帕首。

translations.literal: At the time the wife of Prince of Run Yuanfen, Grand Lady of An State of the Li clan, was old and her hair was falling; seeing the Empress Dowager, she too requested a headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the wife of Prince of Run Yuanfen, Grand Lady of An of the Li clan, was old and her hair was falling out; when she saw the Empress Dowager she too asked for a headcloth.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「大長公主，太宗皇帝女，先帝諸妹也；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "The Grand Elder Princess is Emperor Taizong's daughter, the former emperor's sisters;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "The Grand Elder Princess is Emperor Taizong's daughter, the former emperor's sisters;

sentences.zh: 若趙家老婦，寧可比耶？

translations.literal: how can an old woman of the Zhao house be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: how can an old woman of the Zhao house be compared?"

sentences.zh: 」舊賜大臣茶，有龍鳳飾，太后曰：「此豈人臣可得？

translations.literal: " Tea formerly granted to chief ministers bore dragon and phoenix ornament; the Empress Dowager said, "How can subjects obtain this?"
translations.idiomatic: Tea formerly granted to chief ministers bore dragon and phoenix ornament. The Empress Dowager said, "How can subjects obtain this?"

sentences.zh: 」命有司別制入香京挺以賜之。

translations.literal: " She ordered the responsible offices separately to make fragrant Jingting tribute tea for granting.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the responsible offices to prepare a separate grade of fragrant Jingting tribute tea for granting to them.

sentences.zh: 賜族人御食，必易以釦器，曰：「尚方器勿使入吾家也。

translations.literal: When granting kinsmen imperial food, she always exchanged it for studded vessels, saying, "Let not imperial workshop vessels enter my house."
translations.idiomatic: When granting kinsmen imperial food, she always had it served in studded vessels, saying, "Let no imperial workshop vessels enter my house."

sentences.zh: 」常服絁繻練裙，侍者見仁宗左右簪珥珍麗，欲效之。

translations.literal: " She regularly wore plain silk and white silk skirts; attendants seeing Renzong's attendants with jeweled hairpins and earrings of rare beauty wished to imitate them.
translations.idiomatic: She regularly wore plain silk skirts. When attendants saw Renzong's attendants wearing jeweled hairpins and earrings of rare beauty, they wished to imitate them.

sentences.zh: 太后戒曰：「彼皇帝嬪御飾也，汝安得學。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager admonished, "Those are the emperor's consorts' ornaments—how dare you learn from them?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager admonished them: "Those are the emperor's consorts' ornaments—how dare you imitate them?"

sentences.zh: 先是，小臣方仲弓上書，請依武后故事，立劉氏廟，而程琳亦獻《武后臨朝圖》，后擲其書於地曰：「吾不作此負祖宗事。

translations.literal: Earlier, the minor official Fang Zhonggong memorialized requesting that, following Empress Wu's precedent, a Liu clan temple be established, and Cheng Lin also presented the "Picture of Empress Wu Holding Court"; the Empress threw the book to the ground, saying, "I will not do this thing that betrays the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the minor official Fang Zhonggong memorialized asking that, following Empress Wu's precedent, a Liu clan temple be established, and Cheng Lin also presented a picture of Empress Wu holding court. The Empress threw the book to the ground and said, "I will not do this thing that betrays our ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」有漕臣劉綽者，自京西還，言在庾有出剩糧千餘斛，乞付三司。

translations.literal: " There was the transport official Liu Chuo, returning from the capital west, who said that at the granary there was surplus grain of more than a thousand hu and begged to deliver it to the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: There was a transport official named Liu Chuo who, returning from the capital west, said that at the granary there was more than a thousand hu of surplus grain and asked to deliver it to the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 后問曰：「卿識王曾、張知白、呂夷簡、魯宗道乎？

translations.literal: The Empress asked, "Do you know Wang Zeng, Zhang Zhibai, Lü Yijian, and Lu Zongdao?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress asked, "Do you know Wang Zeng, Zhang Zhibai, Lü Yijian, and Lu Zongdao?

sentences.zh: 此四人豈因獻羨餘進哉！」

translations.literal: Would these four men advance by presenting surplus tribute!"
translations.idiomatic: Would these four men advance by presenting surplus tribute!"

sentences.zh: 后稱制凡十一年，自仁宗即位，乃諭輔臣曰：「皇帝聽斷之暇，宣詔名儒講習經史，以輔其德。

translations.literal: The Empress ruled as regent for eleven years in all; from Renzong's accession she instructed chief ministers, saying, "In the Emperor's leisure from hearing and deciding affairs, proclaim and summon renowned scholars to lecture on the classics and histories, to assist his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress ruled as regent for eleven years in all. From Renzong's accession she instructed the chief ministers: "In the emperor's leisure from hearing and deciding affairs, summon renowned scholars to lecture on the classics and histories to assist his cultivation."

sentences.zh: 」於是設幄崇政殿之西廡，而日命近臣侍講讀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon a lectern was set up in the western gallery of Chongzheng Hall, and daily near ministers were ordered to attend lecturing and reading.
translations.idiomatic: A lectern was then set up in the western gallery of Chongzheng Hall, and each day near ministers were ordered to attend lectures and readings.

sentences.zh: 丁謂、曹利用既以侮權貶竄，而天下惕然畏之。

translations.literal: After Ding Wei and Cao Liyong were demoted and banished for contempt of authority, all under Heaven became wary and in awe of her.
translations.idiomatic: After Ding Wei and Cao Liyong were demoted and banished for abusing their power, the realm stood in wary awe of her.

sentences.zh: 晚稍進外家，任內宮羅崇勳、江德明等訪外事，崇勳等以此勢傾中外。

translations.literal: In her later years she somewhat advanced her maternal kin, employing inner-palace Luo Chongxun, Jiang Deming, and others to inquire into external affairs; Chongxun and the rest thereby bent power within and without.
translations.idiomatic: In her later years she somewhat advanced her maternal kin, employing inner-palace officials Luo Chongxun and Jiang Deming to inquire into external affairs; they thereby bent power within and without the court.

sentences.zh: 兄子從德死，姻戚、門人、廝役拜官者數十人。

translations.literal: When her brother's son Congde died, in-laws, disciples, and servants who received office numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: When her brother's son Congde died, several dozen in-laws, disciples, and servants received offices.

sentences.zh: 御史曹脩古、楊偕、郭勸、段少連論奏，太后悉逐之。

translations.literal: Censors Cao Xiugu, Yang Jie, Guo Quan, and Duan Shaolian memorialized in criticism; the Empress Dowager expelled them all.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Cao Xiugu, Yang Jie, Guo Quan, and Duan Shaolian memorialized in criticism, and the Empress Dowager expelled them all.

sentences.zh: 太后保護帝既盡力，而仁宗所以奉太后亦甚備。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had already exerted her utmost in protecting the Emperor, and Renzong's manner of serving the Empress Dowager was also very complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had done her utmost to protect the emperor, and Renzong in turn served her with complete devotion.

sentences.zh: 上春秋長，猶不知為宸妃所出，終太后之世無毫髮間隙焉。

translations.literal: Though the sovereign's years grew long, he still did not know he was born of Consort the Imperial; to the end of the Empress Dowager's life there was not the slightest rift.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor grew to maturity, he still did not know he was born of Consort the Imperial; to the end of the Empress Dowager's life there was not the slightest rift between them.

sentences.zh: 及不豫，帝為大赦，悉召天下醫者馳傳詣京師。

translations.literal: When she was unwell, the Emperor proclaimed a great amnesty and summoned physicians from all under Heaven by urgent relay to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill, the emperor proclaimed a great amnesty and summoned physicians from across the realm by urgent relay to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諸嘗為太后謫者皆內徙，死者復其宮。

translations.literal: All who had formerly been demoted by the Empress Dowager were moved inward; the dead had their offices restored.
translations.idiomatic: All who had formerly been demoted by the Empress Dowager were recalled inward; the dead had their offices restored.

sentences.zh: 其后言者多追詆太后時事，范仲淹以為言，上曰：「此朕所不忍聞也。

translations.literal: Afterward many who spoke pursued slander of affairs in the Empress Dowager's time; Fan Zhongyan spoke on this, and the sovereign said, "This is what I cannot bear to hear."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward many spoke in condemnation of affairs during the Empress Dowager's regency; Fan Zhongyan raised the matter, and the emperor said, "This is what I cannot bear to hear."

sentences.zh: 」下詔戒中外毋輒言。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued warning within and without not to speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued warning officials within and without the court not to speak rashly on the matter.

sentences.zh: 於是泰甯軍節度使錢惟演請以章獻、章懿與章穆並祔真宗室。

translations.literal: Thereupon Military Commissioner of Taining Army Qian Weiyan requested that Zhangxian, Zhangyi, and Zhangmu be jointly enshrined in Zhenzong's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Military Commissioner Qian Weiyan of the Taining Army asked that Empresses Zhangxian, Zhangyi, and Zhangmu be jointly enshrined in Zhenzong's temple chamber.

sentences.zh: 詔三省與禮院議，皆以謂章穆皇后位崇中壺，已祔真宗廟室，自協一帝一后之文；

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Departments and the Ritual Court to deliberate; all held that Empress Zhangmu, honored in the central palace, was already enshrined in Zhenzong's temple chamber, itself conforming to the pattern of one emperor and one empress;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Three Departments and the Ritual Court to deliberate. All held that Empress Zhangmu, honored in the central palace, was already enshrined in Zhenzong's temple chamber, conforming to the pattern of one emperor and one empress;

sentences.zh: 章獻明肅處坤元之尊，章懿感日符之貴，功德莫與為比，謂宜崇建新廟，同殿異室，歲時薦饗，一用太廟之儀，仍別立廟名，以崇世享。

translations.literal: Zhangxian Mingsu occupied the honor of the Kun origin; Zhangyi was touched by the nobility of the sun's omen—their merit and virtue none could be compared with. They held that a new temple should be grandly established, same hall but separate chambers, seasonal offerings using the Grand Temple's rites, and still separately establishing a temple name to honor perpetual sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangxian Mingsu occupied the honor of the Kun origin and Zhangyi was touched by the nobility of the sun's omen—their merit and virtue were beyond compare. They proposed that a new temple be grandly established with the same hall but separate chambers, seasonal offerings using the Imperial Ancestral Temple's rites, and a separate temple name to honor perpetual sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士馮元等請以奉慈為名，詔依。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Feng Yuan and others requested that it be named Fengci; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Feng Yuan and others proposed the name Fengci; the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 慶曆五年，禮院言章獻、章懿二后，請遵國朝懿德、明德、元德三后同祔太宗廟室故事，遷祔真宗廟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingli the Ritual Court said that the two empresses Zhangxian and Zhangyi should follow the Song precedent of Empresses Yide, Mingde, and Yuande jointly enshrined in Taizong's temple chamber, and be transferred for joint enshrinement in Zhenzong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qingli the Ritual Court proposed that Empresses Zhangxian and Zhangyi follow the precedent of Empresses Yide, Mingde, and Yuande jointly enshrined in Taizong's temple chamber, and be transferred for joint enshrinement in Zhenzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 詔兩制議，翰林學士王堯臣等議，請遷二后祔，序于章穆之次，從之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered deliberation by the two academies; Hanlin academician Wang Yaochan and others deliberated, requesting transfer of the two empresses for joint enshrinement, ordered after Zhangmu; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered deliberation by the two academies. Hanlin academician Wang Yaochan and others proposed transferring the two empresses for joint enshrinement after Zhangmu; the proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 李宸妃

translations.literal: Consort Li the Imperial
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li the Imperial

sentences.zh: 李宸妃，杭州人也。

translations.literal: Consort Li the Imperial was a native of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li the Imperial was a native of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖延嗣，仕錢氏，為金華縣主簿；

translations.literal: Her grandfather Yansi served the Qian house as registrar of Jinhua County;
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Yansi served the Qian house as registrar of Jinhua County;

sentences.zh: 父仁德，終左班殿直。

translations.literal: her father Rendé ended as Left Company Palace Duty Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: her father Rendé ended his career as Left Company Palace Duty Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初入宮，為章獻太后侍兒，莊重寡言，真宗以為司寢。

translations.literal: When she first entered the palace she was a maid of Empress Zhangxian, grave and sparing of speech; Zhenzong made her Chamberlain of the Bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: When she first entered the palace she was a maid of Empress Zhangxian, grave and sparing of speech; Zhenzong appointed her Chamberlain of the Bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 既有娠，從帝臨砌臺，玉釵墜，妃惡之。

translations.literal: When she became pregnant, accompanying the Emperor to the terrace by the steps, a jade hairpin fell; the Consort regarded it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: When she became pregnant, she accompanied the emperor to the terrace by the steps; a jade hairpin fell, and the consort regarded it as ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 帝心卜：釵完，當為男子。

translations.literal: The Emperor divined in his heart: if the hairpin is whole, it will be a male child.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor divined in his heart: if the hairpin is whole, the child will be a boy.

sentences.zh: 左右取以進，釵果不毀，帝甚喜。

translations.literal: Those at hand picked it up and presented it; the hairpin indeed was not broken, and the Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants picked it up and presented it; the hairpin was indeed unbroken, and the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 已而生仁宗，封崇陽縣君；

translations.literal: Thereupon she bore Renzong and was enfeoffed as Lady of Chongyang County;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon she bore Renzong and was enfeoffed as Lady of Chongyang County;

sentences.zh: 復生一女，不育。

translations.literal: She again bore a daughter, who did not survive.
translations.idiomatic: She later bore a daughter who did not survive.

sentences.zh: 進才人，後為婉儀。

translations.literal: She was promoted to Talented Lady; later she became Attendant of Graceful Appearance.
translations.idiomatic: She was promoted to Talented Lady and later to Attendant of Graceful Appearance.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，為順容，從守永定陵。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded, she was made Gentle Countenance and accompanied the guard at Yongding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong acceded to the throne, she was given the rank of Gentle Countenance and assigned to attend Yongding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后使劉美、張懷德為訪其親屬，得其弟用和，補三班奉職。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhangxian had Liu Mei and Zhang Huaidé search out her kin; they found her younger brother Yonghe and appointed him to the Three-Rank Attendant Service.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhangxian sent Liu Mei and Zhang Huaidé to seek out her relatives; they found her younger brother Yonghe and appointed him to the Three-Rank Attendant Service.

sentences.zh: 初，仁宗在繈褓，章獻以為己子，使楊淑妃保視之。

translations.literal: At first, while Renzong was in swaddling clothes, Zhangxian took him as her own son and had Consort Yang the Gracious care for and watch over him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Renzong was still in swaddling clothes, Empress Zhangxian took him as her own son and had Consort Yang the Gracious nurse and watch over him.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，妃嘿處先朝嬪御中，未嘗自異。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded, the Consort quietly dwelt among the previous reign's consorts and attendants, never setting herself apart.
translations.idiomatic: After Renzong acceded, the consort lived quietly among the consorts of the previous reign, never distinguishing herself.

sentences.zh: 人畏太后，亦無敢言者。

translations.literal: People feared the Empress Dowager, and none dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: People feared the empress dowager, and none dared speak of the matter.

sentences.zh: 終太后世，仁宗不自知為妃所出也。

translations.literal: Throughout the Empress Dowager's lifetime, Renzong did not himself know he was borne of the Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the empress dowager's lifetime, Renzong did not know that he was the consort's own son.

sentences.zh: 明道元年，疾革，進位宸妃，薨，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingdao, when her illness reached extremity, she was advanced to Imperial Consort; she died at age forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingdao, as her illness worsened, she was elevated to Imperial Consort; she died at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 初，章獻太后欲以宮人禮治喪于外，丞相呂夷簡奏禮宜從厚。

translations.literal: At first, Empress Dowager Zhangxian wished to conduct the funeral outside the palace with the rites due a palace woman; Chancellor Lü Yijian memorialized that the rites ought to be generous.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Empress Dowager Zhangxian wished to bury her outside the palace with the rites accorded an ordinary palace woman, but Chancellor Lü Yijian memorialized that the funeral rites ought to be generous.

sentences.zh: 太后遽引帝起，有頃，獨坐簾下，召夷簡問曰：「一宮人死，相公云云，何歟？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager abruptly led the Emperor to rise; after a moment she sat alone beneath the curtain and summoned Yijian to ask: "One palace woman dies—why is the Chancellor making such remarks?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager abruptly had the emperor rise; a moment later she sat alone behind the curtain and summoned Yijian, asking: "Why all this talk from the Chancellor over one palace woman's death?"

sentences.zh: 」夷簡曰：「臣待罪宰相，事無內外，無不當預。

translations.literal: " Yijian said: "Your subject, who bears guilt as Chancellor, finds nothing within or without that he ought not attend to.
translations.idiomatic: " Yijian said: "I hold the chancellorship at Your Majesty's pleasure; there is nothing within or without the palace that does not fall within my charge.

sentences.zh: 」太后怒曰：「相公欲離間吾母子耶！

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager said angrily: "Does the Chancellor wish to estrange me and my son!"
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager said angrily: "Does the Chancellor mean to come between me and my son!"

sentences.zh: 」夷簡從容對曰：「陛下不以劉氏為念，臣不敢言；

translations.literal: " Yijian calmly replied: "If Your Majesty gives no thought to the Liu clan, your subject dare not speak;
translations.idiomatic: " Yijian calmly replied: "If Your Majesty gives no thought to the Liu clan, I dare not speak of it;

sentences.zh: 尚念劉氏，是喪禮宜從厚。

translations.literal: if Your Majesty still gives thought to the Liu clan, then the funeral rites ought to be generous.
translations.idiomatic: but if Your Majesty still holds the Liu clan in mind, then the funeral rites ought to be generous."

sentences.zh: 」太后悟，遽曰：「宮人，李宸妃也，且奈何？

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager understood and immediately said: "The palace woman is Consort Li the Imperial—what then is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager understood at once and said: "The palace woman is Consort Li the Imperial—what, then, is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」夷簡乃請治用一品禮，殯洪福院。

translations.literal: " Yijian then requested that first-rank rites be used and that she lie in state at Hongfu Chapel.
translations.idiomatic: " Yijian then requested that first-rank rites be observed and that she lie in state at Hongfu Chapel.

sentences.zh: 夷簡又謂入內都知羅崇勳曰：「宸妃當以后服殮，用水銀實棺，異時勿謂夷簡未嘗道及。

translations.literal: Yijian also told Inner Palace Director-in-Chief Luo Chongxun: "Imperial Consort ought to be enshrouded in empress's garb, and the coffin filled with mercury—do not in future say that Yijian never spoke of it."
translations.idiomatic: Yijian also told Inner Palace Director-in-Chief Luo Chongxun: "The Imperial Consort ought to be enshrouded in an empress's garments, with mercury poured into the coffin—do not say later that Yijian never spoke of this."

sentences.zh: 」崇勳如其言。

translations.literal: " Chongxun did as he said.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongxun did as he said.

sentences.zh: 後章獻太后崩，燕王為仁宗言：「陛下乃李宸妃有所生，妃死以非命。

translations.literal: Later, when Empress Dowager Zhangxian died, the Prince of Yan told Renzong: "Your Majesty was borne of Consort Li the Imperial; the Consort died by violence."
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Empress Dowager Zhangxian died, the Prince of Yan told Renzong: "Your Majesty was born of Consort Li the Imperial; she did not die a natural death."

sentences.zh: 」仁宗號慟頓毀，不視朝累日，下哀痛之詔自責。

translations.literal: " Renzong wailed and sobbed, afflicted to the point of collapse; for many days he did not hold court, and issued an edict of deep grief blaming himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Renzong broke into wailing grief until he nearly collapsed; for many days he did not hold court and issued an edict of mourning in which he blamed himself.

sentences.zh: 尊宸妃為皇太后，諡莊懿。

translations.literal: He honored Imperial Consort as Empress Dowager and gave her the posthumous name Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He honored the Imperial Consort as Empress Dowager, with the posthumous title Zhuangyi.

sentences.zh: 幸洪福院祭告，易梓宮，親哭視之，妃玉色如生，冠服如皇太后，以水銀養之，故不壞。

translations.literal: He visited Hongfu Chapel to offer sacrifice and announcement, changed the inner coffin, and personally wept over her; the Consort's complexion was like life, her cap and robes like an empress dowager's—preserved with mercury, thus undamaged.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Hongfu Chapel to sacrifice and mourn, had the inner coffin opened, and wept over her in person; the consort's complexion was as in life, her cap and robes those of an empress dowager—preserved with mercury, and thus undecayed.

sentences.zh: 仁宗歎曰：「人言其可信哉！

translations.literal: Renzong sighed and said: "How can what people say be trusted!"
translations.idiomatic: Renzong sighed and said: "How can one trust what people say!"

sentences.zh: 」遇劉氏加厚。

translations.literal: " He thereafter treated the Liu clan with redoubled favor.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter he treated the Liu clan with redoubled favor.

sentences.zh: 陪葬永定陵，廟曰奉慈。

translations.literal: She was buried beside Yongding Mausoleum; her temple was named Fengci.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried beside Yongding Mausoleum; her temple was named Fengci.

sentences.zh: 又即景靈宮建神御殿，曰廣孝。

translations.literal: At Jingling Palace a spirit-image hall was also built, named Guangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit-image hall was also built at Jingling Palace, named Guangxiao.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，改諡章懿，升祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era her posthumous name was changed to Zhangyi and she was enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era her posthumous title was changed to Zhangyi, and she was enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 拜用和為彰信軍節度使、檢校侍中，寵賚甚渥。

translations.literal: Yonghe was appointed military commissioner of Zhangxin Army and honorary palace attendant; the favors and gifts were exceedingly generous.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe was appointed military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army and honorary palace attendant, with favors and gifts lavish beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 既而追念不已，顧無以厚其家，乃以福康公主下嫁用和之子瑋。

translations.literal: Yet he ceaselessly recalled her and, finding no way to enrich her family further, gave Princess Fukang in marriage to Yonghe's son Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Still he could not stop mourning her; finding no further way to enrich her family, he gave Princess Fukang in marriage to Yonghe's son Wei.

sentences.zh: 楊淑妃

translations.literal: Consort Yang the Gracious
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang the Gracious

sentences.zh: 楊淑妃，益州郫人。

translations.literal: Consort Yang the Gracious was a native of Pi in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang the Gracious was a native of Pi in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖瑫，父知儼，知儼弟知信，隸禁軍，為天武副指揮使。

translations.literal: Her grandfather was Tao; her father was Zhiyan; Zhiyan's younger brother Zhixin served in the palace guard as deputy commander of the Heavenly Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather was Tao; her father was Zhiyan; Zhiyan's younger brother Zhixin served in the palace guard as deputy commander of the Heavenly Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 妃年十二入皇子宮。

translations.literal: The Consort entered the prince's palace at age twelve.
translations.idiomatic: The consort entered the prince's palace at age twelve.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，拜才人，又拜婕妤，進婉儀，仍詔婉儀升從一品，位昭儀上。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded she was appointed Talented Lady, then Handsome Fair Lady, and advanced to Attendant of Graceful Appearance; an edict also raised Attendants of Graceful Appearance to the second court rank, above Bright Appearance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded she was appointed Talented Lady, then Handsome Fair Lady, and advanced to Attendant of Graceful Appearance; an edict also raised Attendants of Graceful Appearance to the second court rank, above Bright Appearance.

sentences.zh: 帝東封、西祀，凡巡幸皆從。

translations.literal: When the Emperor made the eastern feng and western sacrifices, on every imperial tour she accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the eastern feng and western sacrifices, she accompanied him on every imperial tour.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后為修儀，妃與之位幾埒。

translations.literal: When Empress Zhangxian was an Attendant of Cultivation, the Consort's rank was nearly equal.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Zhangxian held the rank of Attendant of Cultivation, the consort's rank was nearly equal to hers.

sentences.zh: 而妃通敏有智思，奉順章獻無所忤，章獻親愛之。

translations.literal: The Consort was quick-witted and perceptive, deferring to Zhangxian without offense; Zhangxian held her dear.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was quick-witted and perceptive, deferring to Empress Zhangxian without giving offense, and Zhangxian held her dear.

sentences.zh: 故妃雖貴幸，終不以為己間，后加淑妃。

translations.literal: Therefore, though the Consort was honored and favored, she never made herself a wedge between them; later she was elevated to Gracious Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, though the consort was honored and favored, she never came between them; later she was elevated to Gracious Consort.

sentences.zh: 真宗崩，遺制以為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong died, his final testament made her Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong died, his final testament made her Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 始，仁宗在乳褓，章獻使妃護視，凡起居飲食必與之俱，所以擁佑扶持，恩意勤備。

translations.literal: At the beginning, while Renzong was at the breast, Zhangxian had the Consort nurse and watch him; in all rising, sleeping, eating, and drinking she was constantly with him—thus embracing, supporting, and holding him up, with tireless kindness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, while Renzong was still at the breast, Empress Zhangxian had the consort nurse and watch over him; in all his rising, sleeping, eating, and drinking she was constantly at his side—embracing, supporting, and holding him up with tireless kindness.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，嘗召其侄永德見禁中，欲授以諸司副使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor acceded he once summoned her nephew Yongde to the inner palace and wished to grant him the deputy commissioner of a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor acceded, he once summoned her nephew Yongde to the inner palace and wished to appoint him deputy commissioner of a bureau.

sentences.zh: 妃辭曰：「小兒豈勝大恩，小官可也。

translations.literal: The Consort declined, saying: "A young boy cannot bear great favor—a minor office will do."
translations.idiomatic: The consort declined, saying: "A young boy cannot bear such great favor—a minor office will suffice."

sentences.zh: 」更命為右侍禁。

translations.literal: " He then appointed him Right Palace Guard Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed him Right Palace Guard Attendant.

sentences.zh: 章獻遺誥尊為皇太后，居宮中，與皇帝同議軍國事。

translations.literal: Zhangxian's testament edict honored her as Empress Dowager to dwell in the palace and deliberate state and military affairs jointly with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangxian's testament edict honored her as Empress Dowager to dwell in the palace and deliberate state and military affairs jointly with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 閣門趣百僚賀，御史中丞蔡齊目臺吏毋追班，乃入白執政曰：「上春秋長，習知天下情偽，今始親政事，豈宜使女后相繼稱制乎？

translations.literal: The Gate Office urged the hundred officials to offer congratulations; Censor-in-Chief Cai Qi signaled the bureau clerks not to join the ranks, then entered to inform the chief ministers: "The Emperor's years are grown; he is versed in the truth and falsehood of all under Heaven and has just begun to govern in person—is it fitting that empresses succeed one another in regency?"
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Office urged the hundred officials to offer congratulations; Censor-in-Chief Cai Qi signaled the bureau clerks not to join the ranks, then entered to inform the chief ministers: "The emperor has come of age and knows the truth and falsehood of affairs under Heaven; he has just begun to govern in person—is it fitting that empresses succeed one another in regency?"

sentences.zh: 」乃詔刪去遺誥「同議軍國事」語，第存后號。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued deleting from the testament the phrase "deliberate state and military affairs jointly"; only the empress dowager title was retained.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict was then issued deleting from the testament the phrase "deliberate state and military affairs jointly"; only the empress dowager title was retained.

sentences.zh: 奉緡錢二萬助湯沐，后名其所居宮曰保慶，稱保慶皇太后。

translations.literal: She was given twenty thousand strings of silk cash to aid her maintenance; the Empress Dowager named her residence palace Baoqing and styled herself Empress Dowager Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: She was granted twenty thousand strings of silk cash for her maintenance; the empress dowager named her residence palace Baoqing and styled herself Empress Dowager Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年，無疾而薨，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou she died without illness at age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingyou she died without illness at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 殯於皇儀殿。

translations.literal: She lay in state in the Hall of Imperial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: She lay in state in the Hall of Imperial Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝思其保護之恩，命禮官議加服小功。
