translations.literal: The Emperor, recalling her protective kindness, ordered the rites officials to debate adding the lesser mourning of xiaogong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, recalling her protective kindness, ordered the rites officials to debate granting the lesser mourning of xiaogong.

sentences.zh: 初，仁宗未有嗣，后每勸帝擇宗子近屬而賢者，養于宮中，其選即英宗也。

translations.literal: At first, as Renzong had no heir, the Empress Dowager repeatedly urged the Emperor to choose among close clansmen someone worthy and raise him in the palace—the one chosen was Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as Renzong had no heir, the empress dowager repeatedly urged the emperor to choose among close clansmen someone worthy and raise him in the palace—the one chosen was Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，言者謂禮慈母于子祭，于孫止，請廢后廟，瘞其主園陵。

translations.literal: When Yingzong acceded, memorialists cited the rite that a nurturing mother receives sacrifice from the son but not from the grandson, and requested abolishing her temple and burying her spirit tablet at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong acceded, memorialists cited the rite that a nurturing mother receives sacrifice from the son but not from the grandson, and requested abolishing her temple and burying her spirit tablet at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 英宗弗欲遽也，下有司議，未上，會帝崩，遂罷。

translations.literal: Yingzong was unwilling to act hastily; the matter was sent down to officials for debate but not yet submitted when the Emperor suddenly died, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong was unwilling to act hastily; the matter was sent down to officials for debate but not yet submitted when the emperor suddenly died, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 后父祖皆累贈至一品，知信贈節度使。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's father and grandfather were both posthumously advanced to first rank; Zhixin was posthumously made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's father and grandfather were both posthumously advanced to first rank; Zhixin was posthumously made military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 知信子景宗，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Zhixin's son Jingzong is treated in the "Biographies of Imperial Affines."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin's son Jingzong is treated in the "Biographies of Imperial Affines."

sentences.zh: 沈貴妃

translations.literal: Consort Shen the Noble
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shen the Noble

sentences.zh: 沈貴妃，宰相倫之孫，父繼宗，光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Consort Shen the Noble was granddaughter of the chancellor Lun; her father Jizong was vice director of the Directorate of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shen the Noble was the granddaughter of Chancellor Lun; her father Jizong was vice director of the Directorate of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，以將相家子被選。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu she was chosen as a daughter of a general-minister household.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong Xiangfu era she was chosen as a daughter of a general-minister household.

sentences.zh: 初為才人，曆美人、婕妤、充媛，至德妃。

translations.literal: She began as Talented Lady, passed through Beautiful Lady, Handsome Fair Lady, and Replete Beauty, reaching Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: She began as Talented Lady, passed through Beautiful Lady, Handsome Fair Lady, and Replete Beauty, and reached Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 為人淑儉不華，帝亦以妃家世故，待之異眾。

translations.literal: In person she was modest, frugal, and unadorned; the Emperor also, on account of her family's standing, treated her differently from the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In person she was modest, frugal, and unadorned; the emperor also, on account of her family's standing, treated her differently from the others.

sentences.zh: 長秋虛位，帝欲立之，有從中沮之者，不果。

translations.literal: With the Chief Consort's seat vacant, the Emperor wished to establish her; someone dissuaded from within, and it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: With the chief consort's seat vacant, the emperor wished to make her empress, but someone dissuaded him from within, and it did not come to pass.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐末，進貴妃。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiayou she was advanced to Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiayou era she was advanced to Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 熙寧九年薨，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xining she died at age eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xining she died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 許出殯其家，車駕臨奠，輟視朝三日，諡昭靜。

translations.literal: She was permitted to lie in state at her family home; the imperial carriage came to offer sacrifice; court was suspended for three days; her posthumous name was Zhaojing.
translations.idiomatic: She was permitted to lie in state at her family home; the imperial carriage came to offer sacrifice; court was suspended for three days; her posthumous title was Zhaojing.

sentences.zh: 郭皇后

translations.literal: Empress Guo
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guo

sentences.zh: 仁宗郭皇后，其先應州金城人。

translations.literal: Empress Guo of Renzong: her forebears were natives of Jincheng in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guo of Renzong: her forebears were natives of Jincheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 平盧軍節度使崇之孫也。

translations.literal: She was granddaughter of Chong, military commissioner of Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: She was the granddaughter of Chong, military commissioner of the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 天聖二年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng she was established as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiansheng she was established as empress.

sentences.zh: 初，帝寵張美人，欲以為后，章獻太后難之。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor favored Lady Zhang the Beautiful and wished to make her Empress; Empress Zhangxian objected.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor favored Lady Zhang the Beautiful and wished to make her empress, but Empress Zhangxian objected.

sentences.zh: 后既立，而頗見疏。

translations.literal: Once the Empress was established, she was rather estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress was established, she was rather estranged.

sentences.zh: 其后尚美人、楊美人俱幸，數與后忿爭。

translations.literal: Later Lady Shang the Beautiful and Lady Yang the Beautiful were both favored and repeatedly quarreled with the Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lady Shang the Beautiful and Lady Yang the Beautiful were both favored and repeatedly quarreled with the empress.

sentences.zh: 一日，尚氏於上前有侵后語，后不勝忿，批其頰，上自起救之，誤批上頸，上大怒。

translations.literal: One day Lady Shang spoke before the Emperor in words offensive to the Empress; the Empress, unable to contain her rage, struck her cheek; the Emperor rose himself to intervene and the Empress accidentally struck his neck; the Emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: One day Lady Shang spoke before the emperor in words offensive to the empress; the empress, unable to contain her rage, struck her on the cheek; the emperor rose to intervene and the empress accidentally struck his neck; the emperor was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 入內都知閻文應因與上謀廢后，且勸帝以爪痕示執政。

translations.literal: Inner Director Yan Wenyin thereupon plotted with the Emperor to depose the Empress and moreover urged the Emperor to show the claw marks to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Director Yan Wenyin thereupon plotted with the emperor to depose the empress and urged him to show the claw marks to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 上以示呂夷簡，且告之故，夷簡亦以前罷相怨后，乃曰：「古亦有之。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed them to Lü Yijian and told him the reason; Yijian also, bearing grudge against the Empress from an earlier dismissal from the chancellorship, said: "There are precedents in antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed them to Lü Yijian and told him the reason; Yijian also, bearing a grudge against the empress from an earlier dismissal from the chancellorship, said: "There are precedents in antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」后遂廢。

translations.literal: " The Empress was then deposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress was then deposed.

sentences.zh: 詔封為淨妃、玉京沖妙仙師，賜名清悟，居長樂宮。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed her as Pure Consort, Transcendent Master of Jade Capital's Sublime Wonder, granted the name Qingwu, and she dwelt at Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed her as Pure Consort, Transcendent Master of Jade Capital's Sublime Wonder, granted her the name Qingwu, and she dwelt at Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 於是中丞孔道輔、諫官御史范仲淹、段少連等十人伏閣言：「后無過，不可廢。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Kong Daofu, remonstrating officials and censor Fan Zhongyan, Duan Shaolian, and ten others submitted at the palace gate: "The Empress is without fault and cannot be deposed."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Kong Daofu, remonstrating officials and censor Fan Zhongyan, Duan Shaolian, and ten others submitted at the palace gate: "The empress is without fault and cannot be deposed."

sentences.zh: 」道輔等俱被黜責。

translations.literal: " Kong Daofu and the rest were all dismissed and censured.
translations.idiomatic: " Kong Daofu and the rest were all dismissed and censured.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，出居瑤華宮，而尚美人亦廢于洞真宮入道，楊美人別宅安置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou she was sent out to dwell at Yaohua Palace; Lady Shang the Beautiful was also deposed to Dongzhen Palace to enter the Way; Lady Yang the Beautiful was housed separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingyou she was sent out to dwell at Yaohua Palace; Lady Shang the Beautiful was also deposed to Dongzhen Palace to enter the Way; Lady Yang the Beautiful was housed in a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 又賜后號金庭教主、沖靜元師。

translations.literal: She was further granted the title Patriarch of the Golden Court and Primordial Master of Tranquil Purity.
translations.idiomatic: She was further granted the titles Patriarch of the Golden Court and Primordial Master of Tranquil Purity.

sentences.zh: 后帝頗念之，遣使存問，賜以樂府，后和答之，辭甚愴惋。

translations.literal: The Emperor rather missed her and sent envoys to inquire after her and gifted her lyrics; the Empress replied in verse, her words deeply sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rather missed her and sent envoys to inquire after her and gifted her lyrics; the empress replied in verse, her words deeply sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗密令召入，后曰：「若再見召者，須百官立班受冊方可。

translations.literal: The Emperor once secretly ordered her summoned in; the Empress said: "If I am summoned again, the hundred officials must stand in formation and I must receive an investiture document—only then."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once secretly ordered her summoned in; the empress said: "If I am summoned again, the hundred officials must stand in formation and I must receive an investiture document—only then."

sentences.zh: 」屬小疾，遣文應挾醫診視，數日，乃言后暴薨。

translations.literal: " When she suffered a minor ailment, Wenyin was sent with a physician to examine her; after several days it was reported that the Empress had suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: " When she suffered a minor ailment, Wenyin was sent with a physician to examine her; after several days it was reported that the empress had suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 中外疑閻文應進毒，而不得其實。

translations.literal: Within and without the court suspected Yan Wenyin of administering poison, but the truth could not be established.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court suspected Yan Wenyin of administering poison, but the truth could not be established.

sentences.zh: 上深悼之，追復皇后，而停諡冊祔廟之禮。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply mourned her, posthumously restored her as Empress, but suspended the rites of posthumous title, investiture document, and enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned her, posthumously restored her as empress, but suspended the rites of posthumous title, investiture document, and enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 慈聖光獻曹皇后

translations.literal: Empress Cisheng Guangxian of the Cao Clan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Cisheng Guangxian of the Cao Clan

sentences.zh: 慶曆八年閏正月，帝將以望夕再張燈，后諫止。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the eighth year of Qingli the Emperor was about to hang lanterns again on the full-moon evening; the Empress remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of the eighth year of Qingli the emperor was about to hang lanterns again on the full-moon evening; the empress remonstrated and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 后三日，衛卒數人作亂，夜趙屋叩寢殿。

translations.literal: Three days later several guard soldiers mutinied and at night broke through roofs and knocked on the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later several guard soldiers mutinied and at night broke through roofs and knocked on the sleeping quarters.

sentences.zh: 后方侍帝，聞變遽起。

translations.literal: The Empress was attending the Emperor when she heard the disturbance and rose at once.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was attending the emperor when she heard the disturbance and rose at once.

sentences.zh: 帝欲出，后閉閤擁持，趣呼都知王守忠使引兵入。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to go out; the Empress closed the door, held him fast, and urgently called Director Wang Shouzhong to lead troops in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to go out; the empress closed the door, held him fast, and urgently called Director Wang Shouzhong to lead troops in.

sentences.zh: 賊傷宮嬪殿下，聲徹帝所，宦者以乳嫗歐小女子始奏，后叱之曰：「賊在近殺人，敢妄言耶！

translations.literal: The rebels wounded palace ladies below the hall; the sound reached the Emperor's quarters; a eunuch reported that a wet nurse was striking a little girl; the Empress rebuked him: "Rebels are killing people nearby—how dare you speak falsely!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels wounded palace ladies below the hall; the sound reached the emperor's quarters; a eunuch reported that a wet nurse was striking a little girl; the empress rebuked him: "Rebels are killing people nearby—how dare you speak falsely!"

sentences.zh: 」后度賊必縱火，陰遣人挈水踵其后，果舉炬焚簾，水隨滅之。

translations.literal: " The Empress surmised the rebels would set fire and secretly sent men with water to follow them; they indeed raised torches and burned the curtains, and the water extinguished the flames as they came.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress surmised the rebels would set fire and secretly sent men with water to follow them; they indeed raised torches and burned the curtains, and the water extinguished the flames as they came.

sentences.zh: 是夕，所遣宦侍，后皆親剪其發，諭之曰：「明日行賞，用是為驗。

translations.literal: That evening, for every eunuch attendant she dispatched, the Empress personally cut a lock of her hair and instructed them: "Tomorrow rewards will be given—take this as proof."
translations.idiomatic: That evening, for every eunuch attendant she dispatched, the empress personally cut a lock of her hair and instructed them: "Tomorrow rewards will be given—take this as proof."

sentences.zh: 」故爭盡死力，賊即禽滅。

translations.literal: " Therefore they strove with all their might to the death, and the rebels were captured and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore they strove with all their might to the death, and the rebels were captured and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 閤內妾與卒亂當誅，祈哀幸姬，姬言之帝，貸共死。

translations.literal: Palace women within the pavilion who had joined the soldiers in the mutiny deserved execution; they begged favored consorts for mercy; a consort told the Emperor and he pardoned them from joint death.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women within the pavilion who had joined the soldiers in the mutiny deserved execution; they begged favored consorts for mercy; a consort told the emperor and he pardoned them from joint death.

sentences.zh: 后具衣冠見，請論如法，曰：「不如是，無以肅清禁掖。

translations.literal: The Empress came before him in full court dress and requested they be judged according to law, saying: "Without this there is no way to purge and cleanse the inner palace."
translations.idiomatic: The empress came before him in full court dress and requested they be judged according to law, saying: "Without this there is no way to purge and cleanse the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 」帝命坐，后不可，立請，移數刻，卒誅之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered her to sit; she would not; she stood and petitioned for many moments; in the end they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered her to sit; she would not; she stood and petitioned for many moments; in the end they were executed.

sentences.zh: 張妃怙寵上僭，欲假后蓋出遊。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang, relying on favor, overstepped protocol and wished to borrow the Empress's ceremonial canopy to go out touring.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang, relying on favor, overstepped protocol and wished to borrow the empress's ceremonial canopy to go out touring.

sentences.zh: 帝使自來請，后與之，無靳色。

translations.literal: The Emperor had her come herself to request it; the Empress gave it to her, with no reluctant expression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had her come in person to ask; the empress lent it willingly, showing not the slightest reluctance.

sentences.zh: 妃喜，還以告，帝曰：「國家文物儀章，上下有秩，汝張之而出，外廷不汝置。

translations.literal: The Consort was pleased, went back and told him; the Emperor said: "The state's cultural relics and ceremonial regulations have ranks above and below; if you spread it out and go forth, the outer court will not accommodate you."
translations.idiomatic: The consort was delighted and went back to tell him. The emperor said, "The state's ritual regalia and ceremonial norms observe strict ranks from high to low. If you unfurl it and go out, the outer court will not receive you."

sentences.zh: 」妃不懌而輟。

translations.literal: " The Consort was displeased and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The consort took offense and gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 英宗方四歲，育禁中，后拊鞠周盡；

translations.literal: Yingzong was just four years old, raised within the Forbidden Palace; the Empress nursed and reared him with thorough care;
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was only four, he was raised within the inner palace, and the empress nursed and tended him with complete devotion;

sentences.zh: 迨入為嗣子，贊策居多。

translations.literal: when he entered as heir-apparent, her supportive counsel counted for much.
translations.idiomatic: and when he was installed as heir apparent, her counsel carried great weight.

sentences.zh: 帝夜暴疾崩，后悉斂諸門鑰置於前，召皇子入。

translations.literal: The Emperor suddenly fell gravely ill at night and died; the Empress gathered all door keys and placed them before her, summoning the princes to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died suddenly of a violent illness one night. The empress collected all the keys to the gates and laid them before her, then summoned the princes inside.

sentences.zh: 及明，宰臣韓琦等至，奉英宗即位，尊后為皇太后。

translations.literal: When dawn came, Grand Councillors Han Qi and others arrived, installed Yingzong upon the throne, and honored the Empress as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the chief ministers Han Qi and others arrived, enthroned Yingzong, and honored her as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 帝感疾，請權同處分軍國事，御內東門小殿聽政。

translations.literal: The Emperor contracted illness and requested she jointly exercise authority over military and state affairs; she held court at the small hall of the Inner East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, he asked that she share authority over military and state affairs; she held court from the small hall at the Inner East Gate.

sentences.zh: 大臣日奏事有疑未決者，則曰：「公輩更議之。

translations.literal: When ministers daily reported affairs with doubts unresolved, she would say: "You gentlemen discuss it further."
translations.idiomatic: When ministers presented business each day and something remained undecided, she would say, "You gentlemen should discuss it further."

sentences.zh: 」未嘗出己意。

translations.literal: " She never offered her own opinion.
translations.idiomatic: " She never imposed her own views.

sentences.zh: 頗涉經史，多援以決事。

translations.literal: She had considerable knowledge of the classics and histories, often citing them in deciding affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in the classics and histories, she often drew on them when deciding matters.

sentences.zh: 中外章奏日數十，一一能紀綱要。

translations.literal: Memorials from within and without numbered dozens daily; she could summarize the essentials of each one.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of memorials arrived daily from inside and outside the court, and she could grasp the gist of every one.

sentences.zh: 檢柅曹氏及左右臣僕，毫分不以假借，宮省肅然。

translations.literal: She scrutinized and restrained the Cao clan and attendants and servants, granting not the slightest indulgence; the palace precinct was austere and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: She kept strict rein on the Cao clan and on palace attendants and servants, granting not the slightest indulgence, and the inner court grew solemn and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，帝疾益愈，即命撤簾還政，帝持書久不下，及秋始行之。

translations.literal: The next summer the Emperor's illness improved greatly; she at once ordered the screen withdrawn and government returned; the Emperor held the edict long without issuing it, and only in autumn was it carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, as the emperor recovered, she ordered the screen withdrawn and handed back power. The emperor long withheld the decree before finally issuing it—not until autumn.

sentences.zh: 敕有司崇峻典禮，以弟佾同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: She ordered the responsible offices to elevate ceremonial rites, and appointed her younger brother Yi Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: She instructed the responsible offices to elevate court ceremony and made her younger brother Yi an associate grand councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，尊為太皇太后，名宮曰慶壽。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager; her palace was named Qing Shou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, she was honored as grand empress dowager, and her residence was named the Hall of Celebrated Longevity.

sentences.zh: 帝致極誠孝，所以承迎娛悅，無所不盡，從行登玩，每先后策掖。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed utmost filial devotion; in every way to receive, welcome, and delight her he held nothing back; when escorting her on outings and sightseeing, he always went before and after to support her arm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was profoundly filial: in receiving, escorting, and delighting her he held nothing back, and on outings he always walked before and after to steady her arm.

sentences.zh: 后亦慈愛天至，或退朝稍晚，必自至屏扆候矚，間親持饍飲以食帝。

translations.literal: The Empress too was loving by nature; if he returned from court somewhat late, she would herself come to the screen to watch and wait; occasionally she personally held out food and drink to feed the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress returned his affection in full measure. If he came back from court late, she would go to the screen herself to watch for him, and sometimes brought food and drink to feed him with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 外家男子，舊毋得入謁。

translations.literal: Men of the maternal kindred, by old rule, were not permitted to enter for audience.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding rule, no man of her maternal clan might enter to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 后春秋高，佾亦老，帝數言宜使入見，輒不許。

translations.literal: The Empress was advanced in years and Yi was also old; the Emperor repeatedly said he should be allowed to enter for audience, but she always refused.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was elderly and Yi was old as well; the emperor repeatedly urged that he be allowed an audience, but she always refused.

sentences.zh: 他日，佾侍帝，帝復為請，乃許之，因偕詣后閤。

translations.literal: One day Yi attended the Emperor; the Emperor again pleaded on his behalf, and she then permitted it; they went together to the Empress's apartment.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while Yi was attending the emperor, the emperor pleaded again and she relented; they went together to her apartments.

sentences.zh: 少焉，帝先起，若令佾得伸親親意。

translations.literal: After a short while the Emperor rose first, as if to let Yi express kinship feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor rose first, as if to give Yi a chance to speak freely as kin.

sentences.zh: 后遽曰：「此非汝所當得留。

translations.literal: The Empress suddenly said: "This is not something you should be allowed to remain for."
translations.idiomatic: The empress cut in: "You ought not to stay here."

sentences.zh: 」趣遣出。

translations.literal: " She hurriedly sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: " She ordered him out at once.

sentences.zh: 晚得水疾，侍醫莫能治。

translations.literal: In her later years she contracted water illness; attending physicians none could cure it.
translations.idiomatic: In her later years she contracted edema, and none of the attending physicians could cure it.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年冬，疾甚，帝視疾寢門，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Yuanfeng, her illness grew severe; the Emperor attended her at the chamber door, not removing his belt to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Yuanfeng her illness turned grave; the emperor kept vigil at her chamber door and did not unfasten his belt even to sleep.

sentences.zh: 旬日崩，年六十四。

translations.literal: After ten days she died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later she died, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 帝推恩曹氏，拜佾中書令，進官者四十餘人。

translations.literal: The Emperor extended favor to the Cao clan, appointing Yi Director of the Secretariat; more than forty people received promotions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor extended favors to the Cao clan, appointing Yi director of the Secretariat and promoting more than forty others.

sentences.zh: 初，王安石當國，變亂舊章，后乘間語神宗，謂祖宗法度不宜輕改。

translations.literal: Initially, when Wang Anshi held power and overturned old regulations, the Empress seized an opportunity to speak to Shenzong, saying the ancestral and imperial laws should not be lightly altered.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Wang Anshi held power and overturned established regulations, the empress took occasion to tell Shenzong that the laws of the ancestors should not be altered lightly.

sentences.zh: 熙甯宗祀前數日，帝至后所，后曰：「吾昔聞民間疾苦，必以告仁宗，因赦行之，今亦當爾。

translations.literal: Several days before the Xining ancestral rites, the Emperor came to the Empress's quarters; the Empress said: "I formerly heard of the people's hardships and always reported them to Renzong, who then granted amnesty accordingly; today you should do the same."
translations.idiomatic: A few days before the Xining ancestral rites, the emperor visited her. She said, "Whenever I heard of hardships among the people I always told Renzong, and he would grant an amnesty accordingly. You should do the same now."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「今無他事。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "At present there is nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "There is nothing of the kind just now."

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「吾聞民間甚苦青苗、助役，宜罷之。

translations.literal: " The Empress said: "I hear the people greatly suffer from the Green Sprouts and Corvée Exemption policies; they should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "I hear the people are greatly burdened by the Green Sprouts and Corvée Exemption policies—they should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 安石誠有才學，然怨之者甚眾，帝欲愛惜保全之，不若暫出之於外。

translations.literal: Anshi indeed has talent and learning, yet those who resent him are very many; if Your Majesty wishes to cherish and preserve him, it were better temporarily to send him outside.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Anshi has genuine talent, but many resent him. If you mean to protect him, you would do better to send him away from court for a time."

sentences.zh: 」帝悚聽，垂欲止，復為安石所持，遂不果。

translations.literal: " The Emperor listened with alarm, nearly about to stop, but was again swayed by Anshi; in the end it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor listened, startled, and was on the point of stopping—but Wang Anshi swayed him again, and nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗有意于燕薊，已與大臣定議，乃詣慶壽宮白其事。

translations.literal: The Emperor once harbored intention toward Yan and Ji, had already settled the plan with great ministers, then went to Qing Shou Palace to inform her of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once set his mind on recovering Yan and Ji. After settling the plan with his chief ministers, he went to the Hall of Celebrated Longevity to tell her.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「儲蓄賜予備乎？

translations.literal: The Empress said: "Are stores and grants prepared?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked, "Are the treasury stores and disbursements ready?"

sentences.zh: 鎧仗士卒精乎？

translations.literal: Are armor, weapons, and troops elite?"
translations.idiomatic: "Are the armor, weapons, and troops in fighting trim?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「固已辦之矣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "They have indeed been prepared."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "All of that has already been prepared."

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「事體至大，吉凶悔吝生乎動，得之不過南面受賀而已；

translations.literal: " The Empress said: "The matter is exceedingly great; fortune and misfortune, regret and trouble arise from action; if successful it is no more than facing south to receive congratulations;
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "The stake is enormous. Fortune and misfortune spring from action; success would mean no more than receiving congratulations as sovereign—

sentences.zh: 萬一不諧，則生靈所系，未易以言。

translations.literal: if by the slightest chance it fails, then the lives of the people are at stake—no easy thing to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: but if anything goes wrong, countless lives hang in the balance, and the cost is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 苟可取之，太祖、太宗收復久矣，何待今日。

translations.literal: If it could be taken, Taizu and Taizong would have recovered it long ago—why wait until today?"
translations.idiomatic: If it could be taken, Taizu and Taizong would have recovered it long ago. Why wait until today?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「敢不受教。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I dare not but accept your instruction."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I shall heed your teaching."

sentences.zh: 蘇軾以詩得罪，下御史獄，人以為必死。

translations.literal: Su Shi offended through poetry and was sent down to the Censorate prison; people thought he would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi gave offense through his poetry and was thrown into the censorate prison; many assumed he would die.

sentences.zh: 后違預中聞之，謂帝曰：「嘗憶仁宗以制科得軾兄弟，喜曰：『吾為子孫得兩宰相。

translations.literal: The Empress, convalescing in bed, heard of it and told the Emperor: "I recall Renzong obtained the Shi brothers through the draft examination and rejoiced, saying: 'I have gained two chancellors for my descendants.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress, confined to her sickbed, heard of it and told the emperor, "I remember when Renzong recruited the Su brothers through the draft examination. He said with delight, 'I have secured two chancellors for my descendants.'

sentences.zh: 』今聞軾以作詩系獄，得非仇人中傷之乎？

translations.literal: ' Now I hear Shi is imprisoned for writing poetry—is it not that enemies have slandered and injured him?"
translations.idiomatic: ' Now I hear that Su Shi is imprisoned for his poems. Surely enemies have slandered him?"

sentences.zh: 捃至於詩，其過微矣。

translations.literal: Searching even to poetry—the fault is slight indeed.
translations.idiomatic: To dredge up a case from mere poetry—the offense is very slight.

sentences.zh: 吾疾勢已篤，不可以冤濫致傷中和，宜熟察之。

translations.literal: My illness is already grave; wrongful and excessive punishment must not be allowed to harm harmonious equilibrium—you should examine it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: My illness is already grave. You must not let injustice and excess disturb the balance of the realm. Examine this carefully."

sentences.zh: 」帝涕泣，軾由此得免。

translations.literal: " The Emperor wept; Shi thereby escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept, and Su Shi was spared.

sentences.zh: 及崩，帝哀慕毀瘠，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: When she died, the Emperor grieved and pined, wasting away, nearly unable to endure mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, the emperor grieved himself nearly to death and could barely bear his mourning.

sentences.zh: 有司上諡，葬於永昭陵。

translations.literal: The responsible offices submitted a posthumous name; she was buried at Yongzhao Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed her posthumous title, and she was buried at Yongzhao Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃

translations.literal: Honored Consort Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang

sentences.zh: 張貴妃，河南永安人也。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Zhang was a native of Yong'an in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang was a native of Yong'an in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖穎，進士第，終建平令。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Ying passed the jinshi examination and ended as magistrate of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Ying passed the jinshi examination and ended his career as magistrate of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 父堯封，亦舉進士，為石州推官卒。

translations.literal: Her father Yaofeng also passed the jinshi and died while serving as judicial assistant of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yaofeng also passed the jinshi examination and died while serving as judicial assistant of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 時堯封史堯佐補蜀官，堯封妻錢氏求挈孤幼隨之官，堯佐不收恤，以道遠辭。

translations.literal: At the time Yaofeng's uncle Shi Yaozuo was appointed to an office in Shu; Yaofeng's wife Lady Qian asked to bring the orphaned young along to his posting; Yaozuo would not take them in and declined on grounds of the long distance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yaofeng's uncle Shi Yaozuo was appointed to an office in Shu. Yaofeng's widow, Lady Qian, asked to bring the orphaned children to join him, but Yaozuo refused to take them in, citing the long journey.

sentences.zh: 妃幼無依，錢氏遂納于章惠皇后宮寢。

translations.literal: The consort was young and without support; Lady Qian then placed her in Empress Zhanghui's palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Left alone as a child, the girl was placed by Lady Qian in the quarters of Empress Zhanghui.

sentences.zh: 長得幸，有盛寵。

translations.literal: When grown she won favor and enjoyed great affection.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age she won the emperor's favor and enjoyed great affection.

sentences.zh: 妃巧慧多智數，善承迎，勢動中外。

translations.literal: The consort was clever and resourceful, skilled at ingratiation; her influence moved court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and shrewd, skilled at winning favor, she wielded influence that reached both within and beyond the court.

sentences.zh: 慶曆元年，封清河郡君，歲中為才人，遷修媛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingli she was enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe Commandery; within the year she became a Talented Lady, then was promoted to Cultivated Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingli she was enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe Commandery; within the year she became a Talented Lady and was then promoted to Cultivated Beauty.

sentences.zh: 忽被疾，曰：「妾姿薄，不勝寵名，原為美人。

translations.literal: Suddenly taken ill, she said: "Your servant's quality is slight and cannot bear a title of favor; I beg to be a Beautiful Lady only."
translations.idiomatic: When she suddenly fell ill, she said, "Your servant's station is low and cannot bear a lofty title; I ask only to remain a Beautiful Lady."

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: " It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Her request was granted.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，進貴妃。

translations.literal: At the start of Huangyou she was advanced to Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangyou she was promoted to Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 后五年薨，年三十一。

translations.literal: Five years later she died, aged thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later she died, at the age of thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 仁宗哀悼之，追冊為皇后，諡溫成。

translations.literal: Renzong mourned her and posthumously enfeoffed her as empress, with posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong mourned her deeply and posthumously enfeoffed her as empress, with the posthumous title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 追封堯封清河郡王，諡景思。

translations.literal: Yaofeng was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qinghe Commandery, posthumous title Jingsi.
translations.idiomatic: Yaofeng was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qinghe Commandery, with the posthumous title Jingsi.

sentences.zh: 而堯佐因緣僥倖，致位通顯云。

translations.literal: As for Yaozuo, through opportune connections he attained eminent rank, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozuo, meanwhile, parlayed his connection into high office—a rise owed to sheer opportunism, it is said.

sentences.zh: 苗貴妃

translations.literal: Honored Consort Miao
translations.idiomatic: Consort Miao

sentences.zh: 周貴妃

translations.literal: Honored Consort Zhou
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhou

sentences.zh: 周貴妃，開封人。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Zhou was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhou was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 生四歲，從其姑入宮，張貴妃育為女。

translations.literal: At age four she entered the palace with her aunt; Honored Consort Zhang raised her as a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of four she entered the palace with her aunt; Consort Zhang raised her as her own daughter.

sentences.zh: 稍長，遂得侍仁宗，生兩公主。

translations.literal: When she grew somewhat older, she came to attend Renzong and bore two princesses.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew older she came to attend Renzong and bore two princesses.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，妃日一疏食，屏處一室，誦佛書，困則假寐，覺則復誦，晝夜不解衣者四十年。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, the consort took one sparse meal daily, secluded herself in one room, recited Buddhist scriptures; when weary she would doze, when awake she recited again—for forty years day and night she did not remove her clothes.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death she ate one plain meal a day, shut herself in a single room, and recited Buddhist scriptures—dozing when weary, resuming when awake—for forty years she did not undress day or night.

sentences.zh: 公主下嫁錢景臻、郭獻卿。

translations.literal: The princesses married Qian Jingzhen and Guo Xianqing.
translations.idiomatic: The princesses married Qian Jingzhen and Guo Xianqing.

sentences.zh: 連進至賢妃，徽宗立，加貴妃。

translations.literal: She was promoted in succession to Virtuous Consort; when Huizong ascended the throne, she was further advanced to Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: She rose in succession to Virtuous Consort, and when Huizong took the throne she was further promoted to Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 曆五朝，勤約一致。

translations.literal: She passed through five reigns, frugal and consistent throughout.
translations.idiomatic: She lived through five reigns, steadfast in frugality throughout.

sentences.zh: 啟壽藏于周氏塋南，傍建僧屋，費緡錢六萬，皆貯儲奉賜。

translations.literal: She opened a longevity vault south of the Zhou family grave, built a monk's hall beside it, costing sixty thousand strings of cash—all from stored stipends and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: She opened a longevity vault south of the Zhou family cemetery and built a monks' hall beside it at a cost of sixty thousand strings of cash, all drawn from stored stipends and imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 郭公主先亡，詔許出外第，與親戚相往來。

translations.literal: When Princess Guo died first, an edict permitted her to live in an outer residence and visit with relatives.
translations.idiomatic: After Princess Guo died, an edict allowed her to live in an outer residence and receive visits from relatives.

sentences.zh: 年九十三薨，諡昭淑。

translations.literal: She died at ninety-three; posthumous title Zhaoshu.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of ninety-three and was given the posthumous title Zhaoshu.

sentences.zh: 楊德妃

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Yang
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang De

sentences.zh: 楊德妃，定陶人。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Yang was a native of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang De was a native of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，以章獻太后姻連，選為御侍，封原武郡君，進美人。

translations.literal: During Tiansheng, through kinship with Empress Dowager Zhangxian, she was selected as an imperial attendant, enfeoffed Lady of Yuanwu Commandery, and advanced to Beautiful Lady.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era, through kinship with Empress Dowager Zhangxian, she was chosen as an imperial attendant, enfeoffed as Lady of Yuanwu Commandery, and promoted to Beautiful Lady.

sentences.zh: 端麗機敏，妙音律，組紃、書藝一過目如素習。

translations.literal: Comely and quick-witted, skilled in music, embroidery, and calligraphy—one glance and she handled them as if long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful and quick-witted, she excelled at music, embroidery, and calligraphy; anything she saw once she handled as if she had practiced it for years.

sentences.zh: 父忠為侍禁，仁宗欲加獎擢，辭曰：「外官當積勞以取貴，今以恩澤徼幸，恐啟左右詖謁之端。

translations.literal: Her father Zhong served as palace guard; Renzong wished to reward and promote him; he declined, saying: "An outer official should accumulate merit to win honor; now to seek rank through grace and favor would fear opening a door to importunate pleading by those around the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhong was a palace guard. When Renzong wished to reward and promote him, he declined: "An official outside the palace should earn rank through merit. To seek advancement by favor would open the door to importunate pleading at court."

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，命徙居肅儀殿。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was pleased and ordered her moved to reside in the Hall of Solemn Rites.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased and ordered her moved to the Hall of Solemn Rites.

sentences.zh: 贈其祖貴州刺史，而官其叔弟五人。

translations.literal: He posthumously enfeoffed her grandfather as prefect of Guizhou and gave offices to five of her uncles and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously enfeoffed her grandfather as prefect of Guizhou and appointed five of her uncles and younger brothers to office.

sentences.zh: 積與郭后不相能，后既廢，妃亦遣出。

translations.literal: Over time she could not get along with Empress Guo; after the Empress was deposed, the consort was also sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Over time she fell out with Empress Guo; after the empress was deposed, the consort was sent out of the palace as well.

sentences.zh: 后復召為婕妤，曆修媛、修儀。

translations.literal: The Empress later recalled her as Lady of Handsome Fairness; she passed through Cultivated Beauty and Cultivated Dignity.
translations.idiomatic: The empress later recalled her as Lady of Handsome Fairness, and she rose through Cultivated Beauty and Cultivated Dignity.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年薨，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining she died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xining she died, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈德妃。

translations.literal: She was posthumously enfeoffed Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously enfeoffed as Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 馮賢妃

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Feng
translations.idiomatic: Consort Feng Xian

sentences.zh: 宣仁聖烈高皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xuanren Shenlie of the Gao clan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanren Shenlie of the Gao Clan

sentences.zh: 英宗宣仁聖烈高皇后，亳州蒙城人。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanren Shenlie of the Gao clan, consort of Yingzong, was a native of Mengcheng in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanren Shenlie of the Gao clan, consort of Yingzong, was a native of Mengcheng in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖瓊，祖繼勳，皆有勳王室，至節度使。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Qiong and grandfather Jixun both had merit to the royal house, reaching the rank of military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Qiong and grandfather Jixun both served the dynasty with distinction, rising to the rank of military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 母曹氏，慈聖光獻后姊也，故后少鞠宮中。

translations.literal: Her mother was of the Cao clan, elder sister of Empress Cisheng Guangxian; therefore the Empress was raised in the palace from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was a Cao, elder sister of Empress Cisheng Guangxian, so the future empress was raised in the palace from childhood.

sentences.zh: 時英宗亦在帝所，與后年同，仁宗謂慈聖，異日必以為配。

translations.literal: At the time Yingzong was also at the Emperor's side, the same age as the Empress; Renzong told Cisheng that one day they would surely be paired.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong was also at court then, the same age as she; Renzong told Empress Cisheng that the two were destined to be matched.

sentences.zh: 既長，遂成昏濮邸。

translations.literal: When grown, they were married at the Prince of Pu's residence.
translations.idiomatic: When they came of age, they were married at the residence of the Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 生神宗皇帝、岐王顥、嘉王頵、壽康公主。

translations.literal: She bore Emperor Shenzong, Prince of Qi Hao, Prince of Jia Yun, and the Princess of Shoukang.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Emperor Shenzong, Prince Hao of Qi, Prince Yun of Jia, and the Princess of Shoukang.

sentences.zh: 治平二年冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping she was enfeoffed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiping she was enfeoffed as empress.

sentences.zh: 后弟內殿崇班士林，供奉久，帝欲遷其官，后謝曰：「士林獲升朝籍，分量已過，豈宜援先后家比？

translations.literal: The Empress's younger brother Shilin, an Inner Hall honored officer, had long served in attendance; the Emperor wished to transfer his office; the Empress declined, saying: "Shilin has gained entry to the court rolls; his allotment already exceeds measure—how should one cite empresses past and present in comparison?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress's younger brother Shilin, an Inner Hall honored officer, had long served at court. When the emperor wished to promote him, she declined: "Shilin already holds a place at court; his share is more than enough. How can I measure against the families of empresses past and present?"

sentences.zh: 」辭之。

translations.literal: " She refused it.
translations.idiomatic: " She refused.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，尊為皇太后，居寶慈宮。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager and resided at Bao Ci Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, she was honored as empress dowager and took up residence at Bao Ci Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝累欲為高氏營大第，后不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly wished to build a great mansion for the Gao clan; the Empress would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly wanted to build a grand mansion for the Gao clan, but the empress would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 久之，但斥望春門外隙地以賜，凡營繕百役費，悉出寶慈，不調大農一錢。

translations.literal: After a long time, he merely allotted vacant land outside Wangchun Gate; all costs of construction and labor were paid from Bao Ci, not one cash drawn from the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he allotted only vacant land outside Wangchun Gate. Every cost of construction and labor came from Bao Ci Palace—not a single coin from the state treasury.

sentences.zh: 元豐八年，帝不豫，浸劇，宰執王珪等入問疾，乞立延安郡王為皇太子，太后權同聽政，帝頷之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng the Emperor was unwell, growing worse; Grand Councillors Wang Gui and others entered to inquire after his illness, requesting that the Prince of Yan'an be established as crown prince and the Empress Dowager exercise authority to hear government jointly; the Emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng the emperor fell gravely ill. Chief ministers Wang Gui and others came to inquire after him and asked that the Prince of Yan'an be made crown prince and the empress dowager govern jointly behind the screen; the emperor nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 珪等見太后簾下。

translations.literal: Gui and others saw the Empress Dowager below the screen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui and the others met the empress dowager behind the screen.

sentences.zh: 后泣，撫王曰：「兒孝順，自官家服藥，未嘗去左右，書佛經以祈福，喜學書，已誦《論語》七卷，絕不好弄。

translations.literal: The Empress wept, stroking the prince, saying: "The child is filial; since His Majesty took medicine he has never left his side, copies Buddhist scriptures to seek blessing, delights in learning calligraphy, has already recited seven scrolls of the Analects, and utterly dislikes play."
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she stroked the prince and said, "This child is filial. Since His Majesty fell ill he has never left his side. He copies Buddhist scriptures for blessing, loves calligraphy, has already recited seven scrolls of the Analects, and has no taste for idle play."

sentences.zh: 」乃令王出簾外見珪等，珪等再拜謝且賀。

translations.literal: " She then had the prince come outside the screen to meet Gui and others; Gui and others bowed twice in thanks and congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: " She then had the prince come out from behind the screen to meet Wang Gui and the others, who bowed twice in thanks and congratulation.

sentences.zh: 是日降制，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: That day an edict was issued establishing him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict was issued making him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，岐、嘉二王日問起居，至是，令毋輒入。

translations.literal: Initially the two princes of Qi and Jia daily inquired after the Emperor's health; at this time they were ordered not to enter casually.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the princes of Qi and Jia had visited daily to inquire after the emperor's health; now they were forbidden to enter at will.

sentences.zh: 又陰敕中人梁惟簡，使其妻制十歲兒一黃袍，懷以來，蓋密為踐阼倉卒備也。

translations.literal: She also secretly ordered the eunuch Liang Weijian to have his wife make a yellow robe for a ten-year-old boy and bring it hidden on her person—covert preparation in case enthronement came in haste.
translations.idiomatic: She also secretly instructed the eunuch Liang Weijian to have his wife sew a yellow robe for a ten-year-old boy and bring it concealed on her person—a quiet safeguard against a hurried succession.

sentences.zh: 哲宗嗣位，尊為太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Zhezong succeeded to the throne, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong succeeded to the throne, she was honored as grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 驛召司馬光、呂公著，未至，迎問今日設施所宜先。

translations.literal: By express post she summoned Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu; before they arrived, she asked what measures should be taken first today.
translations.idiomatic: She summoned Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu by express courier. Before they arrived, she asked what reforms should come first.

sentences.zh: 未及條上，已散遣修京城役夫，減皇城覘卒，止禁庭工技，廢導洛司，出近侍尤亡狀者。

translations.literal: Before items could be listed and submitted, she had already dismissed laborers repairing the capital, reduced scouts of the Imperial City, halted palace artisans, abolished the Office of the Luoyang Canal, and expelled especially disreputable close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Before any formal list could be submitted, she had already dismissed laborers repairing the capital, reduced imperial-city scouts, halted palace artisans, abolished the Office of the Luoyang Canal, and expelled the worst of the close attendants.

sentences.zh: 戒中外毋苛斂，寬民間保戶馬。

translations.literal: She admonished inner and outer not to levy harshly, and eased the people's obligation of registered household horses.
translations.idiomatic: She warned officials throughout the realm against harsh levies and eased the people's obligation to supply registered household horses.

sentences.zh: 事由中旨，王珪等弗預知。

translations.literal: These matters proceeded by inner edict; Wang Gui and others were not forewarned.
translations.idiomatic: These orders came directly from her; Wang Gui and the others had no advance notice.

sentences.zh: 又起文彥博於既老，遣使勞諸途，諭以復祖宗法度為先務，且令亟疏可用者。

translations.literal: She also recalled Wen Yanbo though already aged, sent envoys to comfort him on the road, instructing him that restoring the ancestral laws was the first task, and ordered him quickly to memorialize usable men.
translations.idiomatic: She also recalled Wen Yanbo, though he was already old, sent envoys to greet him along the road, told him that restoring the laws of the ancestors was the first priority, and ordered him to recommend capable men at once.

sentences.zh: 從父遵裕坐西征失律抵罪，蔡確欲獻諛以固位，乞復其官。

translations.literal: Her father's younger cousin Zunyu was punished for military failure on the western campaign; Cai Que wished to offer flattery to secure his position and requested restoration of his office.
translations.idiomatic: Her father's younger cousin Zunyu had been punished for misconduct on the western campaign. Cai Que, seeking to flatter his way into favor, asked that Zunyu's office be restored.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「遵裕靈武之役，塗炭百萬，先帝中夜得報，起環榻行，徹旦不能寐，聖情自是驚悸，馴致大故，禍由遵裕，得免刑誅，幸矣。

translations.literal: The Empress said: "In Zunyu's Lingwu campaign a million people were ravaged; the late Emperor received the report at midnight, rose and walked around his couch, and until dawn could not sleep; from that shock his health declined, leading to his death—the disaster arose from Zunyu; to escape execution was already fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "In Zunyu's campaign at Lingwu a million people were ruined. The late emperor received word at midnight, rose and paced beside his bed, and could not sleep until dawn. The shock wore on him until it brought on his death. The blame lies with Zunyu—sparing him execution was mercy enough.

sentences.zh: 先帝肉未冷，吾何敢顧私恩而違天下公議！

translations.literal: The late Emperor's flesh is not yet cold—how dare I favor private kindness and defy public opinion under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's body is scarcely cold. How dare I show private favor and defy the judgment of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 」確悚慄而止。

translations.literal: " Que trembled and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Cai Que withdrew, shaken.

sentences.zh: 光、公著至，並命為相，使同心輔政，一時知名士匯進于廷。

translations.literal: When Guang and Gongzhu arrived, both were appointed chancellors and charged to assist in government with one mind; renowned scholars of the time poured into court.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu arrived, both were made chancellors and charged to govern in concert; distinguished scholars of the day flooded into court.

sentences.zh: 凡熙寧以來政事弗便者，次第罷之。

translations.literal: All policies since Xining that were inconvenient were abolished in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Every policy of the Xining era that had proved burdensome was repealed in turn.

sentences.zh: 於是以常平舊式改青苗，以嘉祐差役參募役，除市易之法，逭茶鹽之禁，舉邊砦不毛之地以賜西戎，而宇內復安。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Green Sprouts was changed back to the old Ever-Normal form, the Corvée Exemption was adjusted by the Jiayou corvée system, the Market Exchange law was removed, tea and salt monopolies were relaxed, and barren border garrison lands were granted to the Western Rong—and within the realm peace returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Green Sprouts system was restored to the old Ever-Normal granary model, the Corvée Exemption was revised along Jiayou lines, the Market Exchange law was abolished, tea and salt restrictions were eased, and barren border garrison lands were granted to the Western tribes—and the realm settled again.

sentences.zh: 契丹主戒其臣下，復勿生事於疆場，曰：「南朝盡行仁宗之政矣。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler admonished his ministers, again not to stir trouble on the border, saying: "The Southern Court is fully restoring Renzong's policies."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler warned his ministers not to provoke trouble on the frontier, saying, "The Southern Court is restoring the policies of Renzong in full."

sentences.zh: 蔡確坐《車蓋亭詩》謫嶺表，后謂大臣曰：「元豐之末，吾以今皇帝所書佛經出示人，是時惟王珪曾奏賀，遂定儲極。

translations.literal: Cai Que was demoted to the southern marches for the Carriage-Pavilion Poem; the Empress told great ministers: "At the end of Yuanfeng I showed people the Buddhist scriptures written by the present Emperor; at that time only Wang Gui submitted congratulations of felicitation, and the heir was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que was banished to the far south over the Carriage-Pavilion Poem. The empress told the chief ministers, "At the end of Yuanfeng I showed others the Buddhist scriptures the present emperor had copied. Only Wang Gui offered congratulations then, and the succession was settled.

sentences.zh: 且以子繼父，有何間言？

translations.literal: Moreover, a son succeeding a father—what room for dispute?"
translations.idiomatic: A son succeeding his father—what grounds for quarrel could there be?"

sentences.zh: 而確自謂有定策大功，妄扇事端，規為異時眩惑地。

translations.literal: Yet Que claimed for himself great merit in settling the succession, wantonly stirred up trouble, and plotted ground for future confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cai Que claimed credit for fixing the succession, stirred up trouble without cause, and laid groundwork to confuse matters later.

sentences.zh: 吾不忍明言，姑托訕上為名逐之耳。

translations.literal: I could not bear to speak plainly; I merely used slander of the sovereign as pretext to banish him.
translations.idiomatic: I could not bring myself to say this openly; I banished him only on the pretext of slandering the throne.

sentences.zh: 此宗社大計，奸邪怨謗所不暇恤也。」

translations.literal: This is a great plan for the altars of state—slander from the wicked we have no leisure to heed."
translations.idiomatic: This was a matter of dynastic survival; I had no time to worry about the grumbling of the wicked."

sentences.zh: 廷試舉人，有司請循天聖故事，帝后皆御殿，后止之。

translations.literal: At the palace examination for presented scholars, the responsible offices requested following the Tiansheng precedent that both Emperor and Empress hold court; the Empress stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination, officials asked to follow the Tiansheng precedent of having both emperor and empress hold court; the empress refused.

sentences.zh: 又請受冊寶於文德，后曰：「母后當陽，非國家美事，況天子正衙，豈所當御？

translations.literal: They also requested receiving the seal and regalia at Wende Hall; the Empress said: "An empress dowager holding court in person is no fine thing for the state; moreover the Son of Heaven's main hall—how should she occupy it?"
translations.idiomatic: They also asked that she receive the seal and regalia at Wende Hall. She said, "An empress dowager presiding in person is no credit to the state—and the Son of Heaven's main hall is no place for her to sit."

sentences.zh: 就崇政足矣。

translations.literal: Chongzheng Hall is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzheng Hall will suffice.

sentences.zh: 」上元燈宴，后母當入觀，止之曰：「夫人登樓，上必加禮，是由吾故而越黃制，於心殊不安。

translations.literal: " At the Lantern Festival banquet, the Empress's mother was to enter for viewing; she stopped it, saying: "If my lady mounts the tower, His Majesty must add ceremony—it would be because of me that yellow regulations are overstepped; my heart would be deeply uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: " At the Lantern Festival banquet her mother was to come and watch. She forbade it: "If my lady climbs the tower, His Majesty must add ceremony. Because of me imperial protocol would be breached, and I would be deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 」但令賜之燈燭，遂歲以為常。

translations.literal: " She merely had lanterns and candles bestowed on her, and this became the annual custom.
translations.idiomatic: " She had only lanterns and candles sent to her instead, and that became the yearly custom.

sentences.zh: 侄公繪、公紀當轉觀察使，力遏之。

translations.literal: Her nephews Gonghui and Gongji were due for transfer to regimental commissioner; she forcefully blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Her nephews Gonghui and Gongji were due for promotion to regimental commissioner; she firmly blocked it.

sentences.zh: 帝請至再，僅遷一秩，終后之世不敢改。

translations.literal: The Emperor pleaded repeatedly; they received only one rank's advancement, and throughout her lifetime he did not dare change it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pleaded again and again; they gained only one step in rank, and for the rest of her life he did not dare alter it.

sentences.zh: 又以官冗當汰，詔損外氏恩四之一，以為宮掖先。

translations.literal: Also, since official ranks were redundant and should be trimmed, an edict reduced maternal kin favors by one fourth, taking the inner palace as the first example.
translations.idiomatic: When official ranks proved redundant and due for trimming, she issued an edict cutting maternal-kin favors by one quarter, beginning with the inner palace as her own example.

sentences.zh: 臨政九年，朝廷清明，華夏綏定。

translations.literal: She held government nine years; court was clear and bright, and China was pacified and settled.
translations.idiomatic: She governed for nine years; the court was clear, and the realm was calm and secure.

sentences.zh: 宋用臣等既被斥，祈神宗乳媼入言之，冀得復用。

translations.literal: Song Yongchen and others, having been dismissed, begged Shenzong's wet nurse to enter and speak for them, hoping to be restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yongchen and others, having been dismissed, persuaded Shenzong's wet nurse to intercede for them, hoping to be restored to office.

sentences.zh: 后見其來，曰：「汝來何為？

translations.literal: When the Empress saw her come, she said: "Why have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: When the empress saw her arrive, she said, "Why have you come?"

sentences.zh: 得非為用臣等遊說乎？

translations.literal: Is it not to lobby on behalf of Yongchen and the others?"
translations.idiomatic: Surely you have come to plead for Yongchen and the others?"

sentences.zh: 且汝尚欲如曩日，求內降干撓國政耶？

translations.literal: Do you still wish, as in days past, to seek inner edicts and meddle in state affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you still mean, as in the old days, to seek private edicts from within and interfere in state affairs?"

sentences.zh: 若復爾，吾即斬汝！

translations.literal: If you do so again, I shall behead you at once!"
translations.idiomatic: If you try that again, I will have you beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 」媼大懼，不敢出一言。

translations.literal: " The wet nurse was greatly afraid and did not dare speak a word.
translations.idiomatic: " The wet nurse was terrified and did not dare utter a word.

sentences.zh: 自是內降遂絕，力行故事，抑絕外家私恩。

translations.literal: From then on inner edicts ceased; she vigorously enforced precedent and suppressed private favors to the maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: From then on private inner edicts ceased; she enforced precedent strictly and checked favoritism toward her own kin.

sentences.zh: 文思院奉上之物，無問巨細，終身不取其一。

translations.literal: Of items presented by the Wensiyuan, great or small, throughout her life she took not one.
translations.idiomatic: Of the gifts presented by the Wensiyuan, great or small, she accepted not one in all her life.
